blocks.text: A 2020 census tract in north-central Allen County: 28.896 square miles of land, internal point 40.8240378, -84.1599836. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), national tract file. Allen County holds 35 tracts in the 2020 geography. [verified] — same source.

**It is 98.5% of Sugar Creek Township plus a fifth of American Township.** Of its 107 blocks, 90 fall in [Sugar Creek](../place/sugar-creek-township.yml) — 82.1% of the tract's land, 1,192 people — and 17 in [American](../place/american-township.yml) — 17.9%, 408 people. It holds all but 0.372 square miles of Sugar Creek and adds 5.175 of American, so a figure published for this tract and read as Sugar Creek Township's **overstates it by about a quarter** — 408 of 1,600 residents live in the other township. [inference]

blocks.text: The Ohio House district Allen County votes in under the map now in force, adopted by the Ohio Redistricting Commission on 29 September 2023 to govern the rest of the decade. blocks.text: A precinct of 1.548 square miles in northern Lima holding 3,240 people and 756 housing units, internal point 40.778293, -84.105936. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md), layer 58.

**It is where three sources disagree with each other in a way that means something.** Its 908 registered voters are 0.28 per resident, the lowest of the county's 88 precincts against a median of 0.68 and a next-lowest of 0.54. [verified] — [OpenElections](../../catalog/openelections-ohio.md) against TIGERweb block population. One of its 43 blocks holds 1,360 people in **zero** housing units, and set those aside and the ratio is 0.48 — low, and inside the range the rest of the county occupies.
It voted 287 to 234 for Trump over Biden on a 58.4 per cent turnout — nearly the county's most balanced precinct in a county that went 69 to 29. [verified] — OpenElections.

The single precinct covering [Sugar Creek Township](../place/sugar-creek-township.yml), holding 1,231 people and 515 housing units over 24.094 square miles, internal point 40.824171, -84.173844. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md), layer 58.

**It is coterminous with the township.** The township's own gazetteer record gives 24.094 square miles of land and an internal point of 40.824171, -84.173843 — the same figures, differing in the last decimal place of the longitude by about four inches. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md). It is the only one of the county's 88 precincts that is a whole civil subdivision; four others are whole villages, and the remaining 83 are pieces.

nodes.label: The raid on the Allen County jail

properties.location_description: The Allen County jail at Lima, near Main Street.

blocks.text: On the night of 12 October 1933 three armed men walked into the Allen County jail at Lima, shot Sheriff [Jess L. Sarber](../person/jess-l-sarber.yml), freed the prisoner John Dillinger from his cell, locked the sheriff's wife and his deputy in it, stripped the building of its guns and ammunition and drove west out of town. [verified] — [Chronicling America](../../catalog/chronicling-america.md), *The Times-News* (Hendersonville, N.C.), 13 October 1933, page 1, carrying a United Press dispatch datelined Lima.

It is the county's most widely reported hour and the corpus's first event of the twentieth century. Before this node the county's dated happenings stopped in 1885. [verified] — the corpus's own event nodes.

**Why the man was in this county's jail.** Dillinger was being held on a charge of robbing a bank in Allen County — "the Bluffton, O., Commercial Bank of $2200" — and had been brought up from Dayton about a week before. [verified] — same archive, *The Washington Daily News*, 13 October 1933, page 3.

So the night was not a national story that happened to land in Lima. It began with a bank in [Bluffton](../place/bluffton.yml), forty minutes up the road, and the county was holding the man who was charged with robbing it. [inference]
[verified] — same page.

**The same dispatch contradicts itself about how long the sheriff lived.** In its fourth paragraph he "died 20 minutes later in a hospital"; nine paragraphs on, a pedestrian hears shouting, fetches the chief of police, and the sheriff is taken to the hospital "where he died a few minutes later". [verified] — same page. That a wire story can hold both readings in one column is the plainest evidence this corpus has for how a newspaper differs from the records it was built on, and it is the case that produced [two papers printing one dispatch](../../decisions/two-papers-printing-one-dispatch-are-one-witness.yml).

**Who was named.** Harry Pierpont, Charles Makley and Russell Clark were tried at Lima for the murder, and Pierpont was named the trigger man. Sarber himself, before he died, identified his assailant as "Harry Copeland"; officers said they were convinced the right name was Pierpont. [verified] — same archive, *Evening Star* (Washington, D.C.), 13 October 1933, page 10.

**The county tried all three of them, and it took the National Guard to do it.** Three trials at Lima, each about a week, through February and March 1934, prosecuted by Ernest M. Botkin before Judge E. E. Everett, with Ohio National Guardsmen under Brig. Gen. Harold M. Bush holding the town — machine gun nests at the approaches to the jail, another at the end of the cell corridor, sandbag defenses, and nobody admitted without a written order from the sheriff, the prosecutor or the judge. [verified] — same archive, *Evening Star*, 4 March 1934, page 3, and 25 March 1934, page 2.

**How it ended.** Pierpont was found guilty in the early morning hours of 11 March 1934. [verified] — same archive, *Evening Star*, 12 March 1934, page 3. Pierpont and Makley were sentenced to die and Clark, alone, "drew a verdict of guilty with mercy, obligating the court to pronounce sentence of life imprisonment". [verified] — *Evening Star*, 25 March 1934, page 2, whose Lima dateline has an illegible day.

On 22 September 1934 Pierpont and Makley tried to bluff their way off death row at the Ohio Penitentiary with guns carved from soap; guards shot both, and Makley died within the hour. [verified] — *Evening Star*, 23 September 1934, page 2. Pierpont was electrocuted shortly after midnight on 17 October 1934. [verified] — same archive, *The Daily Alaska Empire*, 17 October 1934, page 1. Twelve months and five days after the raid, all three of the men who came into the jail were dead or serving life, and so was the sheriff.

**What it did to this county's government, which is the reason the corpus went looking.** The sheriff's office passed to his son, [Donald F. Sarber](../person/donald-f-sarber.yml). [verified] — same archive, *Evening Star*, 4 March 1934, which calls the dead man "the elder Sarber, who preceded his son as sheriff". See [the two irregular sheriff transitions](../question/two-irregular-sheriff-transitions.yml), the question this event was retrieved to answer.

refusals: This corpus does not establish what the trials cost the county or how they were paid for.
This node does not establish where the jail stood.

blocks.text: **The organic act of 1820, which divided the cession into fourteen counties and laid out Allen as one of them.** [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md), which gives the act's disposition county by county: Allen was "all of the second townships to the northern limits of the organized counties", and the act further provided that it "be attached to Shelby County for judicial purposes". Allen was afterwards attached to Mercer, and stayed attached until [the organization of 1831](../question/when-allen-county-was-organized.yml).

Laying out a county and organizing its government were separate acts in Ohio practice, often years apart. The corpus had reasoned to that from general practice and put the gap at "about a decade"; the record makes it eleven years, and names both counties Allen was attached to in the meantime. [verified] — same source.

**The date within 1820 is April 1.** "Allen County was formed from the Indian Territory April 1, 1820." [verified] — same source, its chapter on Ohio's counties, both scans identical. That chapter is compiled state-history filler rather than the commissioners' record the rest of this node rests on, so the day is carried at the standard of a gazetteer entry and not of a minute book.

**The act passed on February 12, 1820, and April 1 is when it took effect.** "Allen County was erected by act of February 12, 1820, and was organized by act of February 9, 1831." [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1906](../../catalog/miller-allen-county-1906.md), both scans identical. That answers the question this node asked in the sentence it replaces: the 1885 volume's "formed... April 1, 1820" is the effective date, the 1906 volume gives the passage date, and the two are consistent rather than in conflict.

nodes.label: The assembly of the Ford Lima engine plant's ground

properties.location_description: The north-west quarter of section 17, township 3 south, range 7 east — Bath Township, about 3.3 miles north-east of Lima's internal point.

blocks.text: Between 24 August 1955 and 17 August 1956, Ford Motor Company took the ground its Lima engine plant stands on, in five conveyances, all of them recorded in the Recorder's tract abstract for the north-west quarter of section 17, township 3 south, range 7 east. [verified] — [Section Ground book list](../../catalog/allen-county-recorder-section-ground.md), volume 0028A pages 163–166; see [the plant](../site/ford-lima-engine-plant.yml).

**It is the corpus's first dated event since 1933.** The history this corpus can put a day on ran 1818, 1820, 1832, 1848, 1885, 1918, 1933 and then stopped, which the site has been saying in those words. This is the first thing to fill that end of it, and it arrived from a land record rather than from a newspaper. [verified] — the corpus's own event nodes.

**Ford did not buy this ground in its own name first.** DTI Enterprises Inc bought from the National Lime & Stone Company on 2 June 1955 and from a private owner on 24 December 1955, and conveyed to Ford four times between August 1955 and August 1956; a fifth parcel came to Ford directly from two individuals in January 1956. [verified] — same pages.

A company acquiring adjacent parcels over eighteen months and passing them to one manufacturer is the ordinary shape of a site assembly, in which the assembler exists so that the buyer's name does not appear and the price does not move. [inference]

**What it was before.** A quarry. National Quarries Company held it from 1917, conveyed to the National Lime & Stone Company in January 1944, and it was National Lime & Stone that sold to the assembler in 1955. [verified] — same pages.

**What followed, on the same ground.** A mechanic's lien for $91,546.07 was filed against Ford Motor Company by Carlson Manufacturing Inc on 30 September 1957 — a claim for work done, and so the first dated evidence this corpus holds that the plant was being built. [verified] — same pages.

refusals: Whether DTI Enterprises was Ford's agent, and whether it is connected to the Detroit, Toledo & Ironton Railroad that held ground in this same quarter from 1924 to 1943, this corpus does not know.
This node does not establish when the plant opened or when it first made an engine.

nodes.label: The 1885 Lima oil strike

blocks.text: The well at Lima that struck oil in 1885 and opened the Lima–Indiana field. [inference] The drilling was after natural gas, following the Findlay boom to the north; oil is what came up. [inference]

The Lima crude was sour — high in sulphur, and difficult to refine into a saleable illuminant by the methods of the day. That property is why the field's development depended on a desulphurization process and hence on the capital and patents of [Standard Oil](../organization/standard-oil.yml) rather than on local operators. [inference]

The strike `affected` the county and not only the city: the Lima–Indiana field extended well beyond the corporate boundary. [inference] That is why this node carries an `affected` edge to the county alongside its `occurred-in` edge to Lima — the two say different things, and only the first is true of the ground outside the city.

**What the strike did to the county was add, not replace.** This node used to say the county's economy "was reoriented from agriculture to petroleum and the manufacturing that followed it", which was written before the corpus had measured any agriculture at all. It has now. Twenty-five years after the strike, Allen County had 2,939 farms against 2,858 in 1900, 92.5 per cent of its land area in farms, and improved acreage higher than before the boom began. [verified] — [Abstract of the Thirteenth Census, Supplement for Ohio](../../catalog/census-1910-abstract-supplement-ohio.md); see [the county's farms](../measure/allen-county-farms-1900-1910.yml). The farms did not go anywhere. A city grew beside them. [inference]

**The one farm figure that moved sharply is price.** An acre of Allen County farmland went from $38.39 in 1900 to $76.28 in 1910, and all farm property rose 89.0 per cent against 58.7 for Ohio. [verified] — same source, which prints both percentages.

[verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md). A book that catalogues a $12,000 flour mill would not have missed an oil field in the town it is written about. So the strike had not happened, or had not yet registered, when this went to press — which bounds it from below without naming a well, and is the first independent support this corpus has for the year 1885 at all. [inference]

**The conditions the received account requires are all in the book, and the oil is not.** Gas shows across the county; a gas boom at Findlay, whose "two gas wells" the same volume notes; a Lima Gaslight Company with a secretary who married [B. C. Faurot's](../person/benjamin-faurot.yml) daughter in January 1885; and Faurot himself owning the paper mill that needed the fuel. [verified] — same source. The story of a man drilling for gas at his own mill is not verified here, but every one of its preconditions now is.

**The well was completed on May 9, 1885, and it was not looking for oil.** The drill began work in the spring of 1885 on the grounds of the Lima Straw Board Works, on the bank of the [Ottawa River](../natural-feature/ottawa-river.yml), under the direction of [B. C. Faurot](../person/benjamin-faurot.yml); the contractors were Brownyear and Martin. **It was put down for a double purpose** — "they needed a better quality of water and more of it for manufacturing purposes, and they hoped they might possibly get a supply of natural gas", gas having been found shortly before at Bowling Green and Findlay. [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1906](../../catalog/miller-allen-county-1906.md), both scans agreeing on every figure below.

The oil was "dark in color, low in gravity and very offensive in odor", and "to a Pennsylvania oil man, these characteristics seemed to condemn the new supply". [verified] — same source. The water motive is the detail every retelling drops, and it is the one that makes the event legible: a paper mill wanted a better well.

**The famous well failed.** The pioneer well met "a series of misfortunes that left it useless". The Citizens' Gas Company, formed to establish whether there was really oil about Lima, put down a **second** well that autumn, and it is that one "to be credited with yielding the first regular and persistent supply of petroleum from the Trenton limestone in Ohio" — 40 to 45 barrels a day at first, **1,450 barrels in December 1885**, and an average of 26 a day through the first quarter of 1886. Its oil was the first sent to refineries to be tested at scale, and the tests established that Lima crude could be deodorized. [verified] — same source. So the event this corpus named for a single strike is two wells: one that made the discovery and broke, and one that proved the field. [inference]

I. E. Dean, experienced in Canada, was among the first outsiders to arrive and organized the Trenton Rock Oil Company — which within a year held a lease that nearly cost Lima [its refinery](../site/lima-refinery.yml). [verified] — same source and [A Standard History of Allen County, 1921](../../catalog/rusler-allen-county-1921.md).

**The first primary record of the boom reaching a named piece of ground.** On 29 September 1885, four and a half months after the well, an oil lease over part of the north-west quarter of section 17 in [Bath Township](../place/bath-township.yml) — 3.3 miles north-east of Lima's internal point — was granted to **B. C. Faurot and others**, and recorded the following April. It was later released. [verified] — [Section Ground book list](../../catalog/allen-county-recorder-section-ground.md), volume 0028A page 164, lease volume L-3 page 121.

Until now the claim that the field extended beyond the city was an inference from the field's name. This is a dated instrument, on ground the corpus can point at, taken by the man who financed the well, in the September after it came in. [inference] A second oil lease over the same quarter followed on 2 November 1898, also released. [verified] — same pages.

**And there is an earlier one, twenty days after the well.** An oil lease over part of the north-west quarter of section 14 in [Shawnee Township](../place/shawnee-township.yml) — the ground the tank plant stands on now — ran to "B C Faurot Et al" dated **29 May 1885**, recorded 20 July 1886, and was afterwards cancelled. [verified] — same source, volume 0034A page 89, lease volume 3 page 410. The well came in on 9 May. [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1906](../../catalog/miller-allen-county-1906.md).

So within three weeks of the strike its financier was taking oil rights four miles south of the city, and by that September four miles north-east of it. [inference] The two leases are the only record this corpus holds of what the boom did in its first months, and what it did was move across the county in both directions almost at once. [inference]

**Others followed, and then Standard's operating company.** A second lease over the section 14 quarter went to H M Earnst in February 1886; the **Ohio Oil Company** took four leases over it between September 1895 and September 1897 and three rights of way in April 1907. [verified] — same pages.

Both Faurot leases were released or cancelled, so neither says anything about whether oil was found there. A lease is a record of where people expected oil, which is a different and in some ways more useful fact. [inference]

refusals: **A source printed in 1885 does not know this happened, and that is evidence.** The county history published that year is exhaustive about Lima's industry — it names the paper mills, the machine works, the iron fence company, the egg-carrier patent, the gas works, every bank and the year each was organized.

nodes.label: Removal of the Ottawa from the Auglaize and Ottawa river reserves

blocks.text: The removal of the Ottawa from their reserved lands in and near this county to territory west of the Mississippi, following further cession in the early 1830s. [inference]

nodes.label: The renaming of German Township

properties.location_description: German Township, Allen County, by order of the county commissioners.

blocks.text: On 16 August 1918 the Allen County commissioners, acting on a citizens' petition, changed the name of German Township to [American Township](../place/american-township.yml). [verified] — [A Standard History of Allen County, 1921](../../catalog/rusler-allen-county-1921.md).

The petition's stated ground was formal: Article II says only "that good cause is shown why the name of said township should be changed", and stipulates that the change "shall in no wise affect the right of property, or the internal concerns of said township". The historian who prints it reads the language for what it is — "'good cause' means patriotism" — and records that school books were being reset and businesses were dropping the word. [verified] — same source.

**This node exists because the corpus had the date and no place to put it.** The renaming was established two phases before this one and recorded as prose on a place and a question, which is where an answer goes and not where a happening goes. It was therefore absent from every view built on the event class, including the site's timeline, and its absence made the county's eighteen-eighty-five-to-nineteen-thirty-three gap look wider than the corpus's own knowledge. [verified] — the corpus's own history; see [what became of German and Ottawa townships](../question/what-became-of-german-and-ottawa-townships.yml).

It is one of two Allen County township name changes this corpus knows of, and the only one whose day it has. [inference] The instrument is the same one that erected every township in the county and incorporated every village here: a petition and an order of the county commissioners. [verified] — same source.

refusals: This node does not establish how the vote went or who signed the petition.

properties.location_description: In session at Lima. The act text names no place; the commissioners had met in the court house since 1842. [inference]

blocks.text: The sitting at which the Allen County commissioners redrew every township line in the county at once, "consequent on the formation of Auglaize County". [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md), which resumes the commissioners' record. Both scans carry the act's text identically.

**The county lost its southern half and gained a northern one.** In March 1846 Allen County assessed sixteen townships in four districts, eight of which — Deuchoquette, Moulton, Washington, Pusheta, Clay, Union, Wayne and Goshen — are in Auglaize County today. [verified] — same source, the 1846 assessors' districts. In exchange the act took ground from Putnam and Van Wert Counties: Riley Township's south tier to [Richland](../place/richland-township.yml), the south half of Jennings to [Marion](../place/marion-township.yml), and Salem's north-east quarter with Jennings' east half set off as [Spencer](../place/spencer-township.yml).

**The transfer was settled in cash.** In May 1853 the commissioners of Allen and Putnam met and agreed that Allen owed Putnam **$3,848.76** arising from the changes. [verified] — same source. Two counties reconciling an account five years later is the strongest internal evidence that the 1885 compiler was reading a real record rather than composing one.

**Allen County's population before and after this date is not a series.** The 1885 statistics chapter gives county totals of 578 in 1830 and 9,079, 12,116, 19,185, 23,623 and 31,314 for 1840 to 1880, and footnotes that the marked townships "form a portion of the adjoining county of Auglaize" since the change. [verified] — same source. The 1840 figure therefore counts ground that has not been in this county since 1848, and does not count Sugar Creek, Monroe or Richland, which were Putnam's. Any trend drawn across 1848 is a trend about two different counties — see [the pre-1970 series](../question/pre-1970-population-series.yml).

**A second historian puts a number on it and adds a county.** "When Auglaize County was formed Allen lost on the south and gained on the west and north, annexing something from Mercer, Van Wert and Putnam counties. Through the juggling process **it lost 138 square miles of territory**." [verified] — [A Standard History of Allen County, 1921](../../catalog/rusler-allen-county-1921.md), a single witness read once for the figure. Mercer is a third donor the 1885 act transcript does not name, and 138 square miles is about a fifth of the county's present 404.

nodes.label: The United States buys the tank plant's ground

properties.location_description: The north-west quarter of section 14, township 4 south, range 6 east — Shawnee Township, about 2.8 miles south of Lima's internal point.

blocks.text: Between 20 and 28 June 1951 the United States of America took the north-west quarter of section 14, township 4 south, range 6 east, from five private owners in five warranty deeds — 60.24 acres, 5 acres, 40 acres of the west half of the east half, and two parcels described only as "Pt". Each was recorded on the day it was signed or the day after. [verified] — [Section Ground book list](../../catalog/allen-county-recorder-section-ground.md), volume 0034A pages 89–92, at volumes 320 pages 573, 574 and 577 and 321 pages 245 and 246.

It is the ground the [Joint Systems Manufacturing Center](../site/lima-army-tank-plant.yml) stands on, and this is the corpus's answer to a question that node has carried since genesis. [verified] — same pages and [the survey sections](../measure/allen-county-survey-sections.yml).

**The date is the finding.** The received account of tank building at Lima is a wartime one, and this corpus had assembled its own version of it: the Lima Locomotive Works taking a medium tank contract in 1941, [the Lima Tank Depot](../site/lima-tank-depot.yml) under construction in January 1943. None of that is this ground. Through the whole of that war it was a mortgaged farm — borrowed against in 1940, 1941 and 1944, leased to a fishing and game club in April 1940, and crossed by pipeline rights of way its private owners granted in 1939, 1940 and 1949. [verified] — same pages.
The Army arrived here six years after that war ended, in the second year of the Korean one. [inference]

**Nine days, five sellers, same-day recording.** That is what a government buying to a deadline looks like rather than a farm changing hands, and it is the only thing the record says about how the acquisition was conducted. [inference]

refusals: This node does not establish when anything was built on the ground it describes.

properties.location_description: St. Marys, in present-day Auglaize County, Ohio. [inference]

blocks.text: The 1818 treaty negotiations at St. Marys, Ohio, by which Native nations ceded the remaining lands in northwest Ohio — the cession that made the ground Allen County was later laid out on available for survey and sale. [inference]

The cession also established reservations, including Ottawa reserves on the Auglaize and Ottawa rivers, which were themselves ceded and their occupants removed within about fifteen years — see [the Ottawa removal](ottawa-removal.yml). [inference]

nodes.label: Allen County Court of Common Pleas

blocks.text: **It is divided five ways by its own rules and staffed four.** The court's local rules, adopted under Article IV, Section V(B) of the Ohio Constitution and effective 1 February 2023, govern practice "in the General Trial Division, Criminal Division, Domestic Relations Division, and where applicable, the Juvenile Division and Probate Division". [verified] — [the court's local rules](../../catalog/allen-county-common-pleas-local-rules.md). Four judges are elected, to the [General](../office/judge-of-the-common-pleas-general-division.yml) (two seats), [Domestic Relations](../office/judge-of-the-common-pleas-domestic-relations-division.yml) and [Probate](../office/judge-of-the-common-pleas-probate-division.yml) divisions. [verified] — [Ohio county elected officials lookup](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md). The Criminal Division has no separately elected judge. [inference]

**Three sources divide this court three ways and none of them is wrong.** The rules divide practice into five, the county's site divides it into three offices with their own sites, and the ballot divides it into four seats. They are answers to different questions and the corpus keeps all three rather than picking one. [inference]

Its judges serve six years where every other elected officer of this county serves four. [verified] — same roster; the length is arithmetic on the term dates. [inference] Three of the four terms begin in February and one in January.

Its records are kept by [the clerk of courts](../office/allen-county-clerk-of-courts.yml), an elected county officer who is not part of the court. [verified] — [the clerk's site](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md).

properties.authority_source: Ohio Revised Code 3311.05, which constitutes an educational service center out of a county's territory less its city and exempted village school districts. [verified]

blocks.text: The county's school jurisdiction that is not a school district. Its office is at 1920 Slabtown Road, Lima, and its governing board has five elected members on four-year terms. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**Who governs it now.** Brooke L. Hedges, David Earnest Mayer and Lori M. Ringwald to 31 December 2029, and Ann B. Best and Walter W. Paxson to 31 December 2027; Hedges and Paxson were appointed. [verified] — same source. Two of five is the heaviest use of appointment on any school board in the county. [verified] — [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml).

**The statute defines it by subtraction, which is why it has no boundary of its own.** An educational service center is *"the territory within the territorial limits of a county ... exclusive of the territory embraced in any city school district or exempted village school district"*, with territory detached for school purposes excluded and territory attached for them included. [verified] — [Ohio Revised Code 3311.05](../../catalog/ohio-revised-code.md). So this jurisdiction is Allen County minus [Lima City](lima-city-school-district.yml), minus the Allen part of [Delphos City](delphos-city-school-district.yml), and minus the Allen part of [Bluffton](bluffton-exempted-village-school-district.yml)'s — the three districts here that are not *local* districts.

properties.authority_source: An act of the Ohio General Assembly laying out the county from lands ceded at the Treaty of St. Marys. [inference] — the act itself has not been retrieved.

blocks.text: The county government: the unit of general-purpose government whose territory is [Allen County](../place/allen-county.yml). Ohio counties are administrative subdivisions of the state rather than home-rule corporations. [inference]

**Nine separately elected offices govern Allen County, and eleven people hold them, because the board of commissioners seats three.** [verified] — [Ohio county elected officials lookup](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

Each is now a node: [the board of commissioners](../office/allen-county-board-of-commissioners.yml), which has three members, alongside the [auditor](../office/allen-county-auditor.yml), [treasurer](../office/allen-county-treasurer.yml), [recorder](../office/allen-county-recorder.yml), [sheriff](../office/allen-county-sheriff.yml), [prosecuting attorney](../office/allen-county-prosecuting-attorney.yml), [clerk of courts](../office/allen-county-clerk-of-courts.yml), [coroner](../office/allen-county-coroner.yml) and [engineer](../office/allen-county-engineer.yml). [verified] — same source.

That sentence stood on this node as an untethered `[inference]` for nine phases, naming all nine offices while the corpus held nodes for one of them. See [a deep instance can hide an empty class](../../decisions/a-deep-instance-can-hide-an-empty-class.yml).

**Three courts sit over this ground and none of them is the county government.** [The Court of Common Pleas](allen-county-court-of-common-pleas.yml) is the county's trial court, [the Lima Municipal Court](lima-municipal-court.yml) covers the whole county despite its name, and [the Third District Court of Appeals](third-district-court-of-appeals.yml) covers this county and sixteen others from an office in Lima. Six judges are elected by this county's voters, on six-year terms where every administrative officer serves four. [verified] — [Ohio county elected officials lookup](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**Both bodies that open named are now held, and the roster held them the whole time.** The county's state legislators arrived two phases later; the forty-eight trustees and fiscal officers of the twelve townships arrived when the roster was read across all eighty-eight of its precinct pages rather than one. [verified] — same source.

**What that reading found is a fact about this county's government and not about its townships.** Two hundred and eleven people hold elective office over ground in Allen County, and thirty-nine of the hundred and sixty-six local ones were appointed to the seat rather than elected to it — none of them in this government, twenty-five of them in the seven villages. [verified] — [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml). Every one of the twenty-two county offices and judgeships is filled, and filled by election.

A district of 5,908 people over 72.263 square miles in the east of the county, internal point 40.721894, -83.954012, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

**It is the only one of the twelve whose name is not on any map of the county.** The other eleven carry the name of a village, a city or a township; this one carries the county's name and a compass direction, which is what a district looks like when it is assembled out of ground rather than grown from a town. It spans [Jackson Township](../place/jackson-township.yml) entire (3,143), [Auglaize Township](../place/auglaize-township.yml) all but 17 people (2,740), and 25 people of [Perry Township](../place/perry-township.yml). [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block.

It holds three settlements and no large one: [Harrod](../place/harrod.yml) 423, [Lafayette](../place/lafayette.yml) 406, and [Westminster](../place/westminster.yml) 406 — 1,235 people in named places out of 5,908. [verified] — same source.

**Who governs it now.** Its five board members are Casey Craig Counts, Claire D. Mackey and Crosby L. McDorman to 31 December 2029, and Jason R. Werling and Steven Michael Emerick to 31 December 2027. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**It is the steadiest district in the county.** 1,073 pupils in 2010 and 1,065 in 2023 — a fall of eight, where the twelve together lost 1,872. [verified] — [enrolment](../measure/allen-county-school-enrolment-2010-2023.yml). It spends $10,941 a pupil, second lowest, on 37.0 per cent local revenue and 7.9 per cent child poverty. [verified] — [the finance survey](../measure/allen-county-school-finance-2023.yml) and [child poverty](../measure/allen-county-school-district-poverty-2023.yml).

properties.authority_source: Order of the commissioners of Mercer County, Allen County then being attached to Mercer for judicial purposes. [verified]

blocks.text: The township government whose territory is [Amanda Township](../place/amanda-township.yml). Its township house is at 690 S. Conant Road, its telephone is 419.647.6259, and its trustees meet on the first and third Wednesday of the month at 8:00 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.729304, -84.280797, landmarked `AMANDA TOWNSHIP HOUSE`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

Its house carries a **Spencerville** postal address, and Spencerville is a village in [Spencer Township](../place/spencer-township.yml), not in this one. The county's own address file gives the building a blank `MUNI` — its answer for *in no municipality* — and the coordinate falls inside Amanda Township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md), point-in-polygon against the 2020 county-subdivision layer.

**Erected in 1830 by the commissioners of Mercer County**, a year before Allen County had a board of its own — see [the place](../place/amanda-township.yml). Thirteen electors lived in it and twelve attended the organizing meeting. [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md).

**Samuel Baxter was its first clerk and Daniel Hoak its first justice of the peace**; William Stewart, Samuel Washburn, A. Martin "and others" filled the remaining town offices. [verified] — same source.

**Who governs it now.** Its trustees are Douglas C. Post and Robert Charles Barnt, both to 31 December 2029, and Brad J. Core, whose term the roster runs to 31 December 2027 without giving its start; its fiscal officer is Brenda L. Core, to 31 March 2028. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md). The oldest township government this corpus can date has a present-tense board in it for the first time, a hundred and ninety-six years after the commissioners of another county erected it.

properties.authority_source: Act of the Allen County commissioners of December 6, 1831, under the name German; boundaries extended and the town regularly organized in March 1833. [verified]

blocks.text: The township government whose territory is [American Township](../place/american-township.yml). Its township house is at 102 Pioneer Road, its telephone is 419.331.8651, and its trustees meet on the second and last Monday of the month at 7:30 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.782867, -84.189127, landmarked `AMERICAN TOWNSHIP ADMINISTRATION BUILDING`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

It governs the county's most populous township — 14,538 people, more than any civil subdivision but [Lima](../place/lima.yml) — and the building is landmarked as an *administration building* rather than a township house, which is what a township of that size looks like in a county file. It runs its own fire service from two further addresses on Elida Road and Edgewood Drive, and a third station inside [Elida](../place/elida.yml). [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md).

**Erected December 6, 1831 under the name German**, by act of the Allen County commissioners — the county's third township, and this government's original name — see [the place](../place/american-township.yml). [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md).

**The boundaries were extended in March 1833 and the town then regularly organized**, with John Brand, William Bowman and Samuel Richards elected trustees, **Griffith John** clerk and John Ireland justice of the peace. Griffith John, this township's first clerk, went on to petition for its enlargement, assess its district in 1846 and plat [Elida](../place/elida.yml) in 1852. [verified] — same source.

**Who governs it now.** Its trustees are Jody M. Long and Paul Michael Basinger, both to 31 December 2029, and Ross Michael Harmon to 31 December 2027; its fiscal officer is Brady M. Overholt, to 31 March 2028. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md). Four officers for 14,435 people, which is the county's largest township government and exactly the same four seats [Sugar Creek](sugar-creek-township.yml) fills for 1,398. [verified] — [the race table](../measure/allen-county-race-2023.yml) for both figures.

properties.authority_source: Order of the commissioners of Allen County. [verified]

blocks.text: The township government whose territory is [Auglaize Township](../place/auglaize-township.yml). Its township house is at 7726 Bellefontaine Road, its telephone is 419.648.7144, and its trustees meet on the first and third Monday of the month at 7:30 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.676380, -83.959923, landmarked `AUGLAIZE TOWNSHIP HOUSE & GARAGE`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

Its territory holds two settlements, [Harrod](../place/harrod.yml) and [Westminster](../place/westminster.yml), and it is one of only two civil subdivisions in the county that gained population between 2020 and 2024. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md).

**Established March 5, 1832 by order of the Allen County commissioners** — the first township the county's own board created rather than inherited — see [the place](../place/auglaize-township.yml). [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md).

**Its first township board was Tolson Ford, William Gilmore and James Watt as trustees, with Tolson Ford also justice of the peace** — a board of three in a township whose first cabin was built by John Goode. [verified] — same source.

**Who governs it now.** Its trustees are Michael D. Stout and Stephen Glen Ewing, both to 31 December 2029, and Russell B. Winegardner to 31 December 2027; its fiscal officer is Melissa Renee Marshall, to 31 March 2028. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**One of those four is the only appointed township officer in Allen County.** Winegardner is marked `*Appointed*`, and he is also the only one of the county's forty-eight township officers the roster gives a party. [verified] — same source, and [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml).

A district of 12,101 people over 44.495 square miles north-east of Lima, internal point 40.79708, -84.060212, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

It lies wholly inside Allen County and is **not** the same ground as the township it is named for. All 9,399 people of [Bath Township](../place/bath-township.yml) are in it — 255 of the township's 256 blocks, the exception an unpopulated one that belongs to the Lima City district — but so are 1,573 residents of [Lima](../place/lima.yml) and 1,129 of [Monroe Township](../place/monroe-township.yml). A fifth of the district lives outside its namesake. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block.
It contains one incorporated place, [Cairo](../place/cairo.yml) and its 517 people. [verified] — same source.

**Most of its Lima share is one block with no housing in it.** 1,360 of those 1,573 city residents are in census block `390030112001004`, which holds zero housing units — a group quarters, not a neighbourhood. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block layer. So the number of Lima *households* in this district is nearer 213 than 1,573, and [what stands on that block](../question/who-lives-in-the-county-without-housing.yml) is an open question.

**Who governs it now.** Its five board members are Jessica M. Kelley and Philip C. White to 31 December 2029, and Michael Thomas Leidy, Rick Allen Kennedy Jr. and Stephanie A. Ernest to 31 December 2027. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

1,692 pupils in 2023 against 1,803 in 2010; $12,305 of current spending a pupil, 53.4 per cent of revenue local; 12.4 per cent child poverty. [verified] — [enrolment](../measure/allen-county-school-enrolment-2010-2023.yml), [the finance survey](../measure/allen-county-school-finance-2023.yml) and [child poverty](../measure/allen-county-school-district-poverty-2023.yml).

The township government whose territory is [Bath Township](../place/bath-township.yml). Its township house is at 2880 Ada Road, its telephone is 419.221.1797, and its trustees meet on the first and third Tuesday of the month at 7:00 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.759189, -84.051832, landmarked `BATH TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

The county's address file landmarks the building as `BATH TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES` and a township garage at the same address. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md). That landmark is the closest thing in any retrieved source to a statement that the board exists as a body with a place to sit.
Its postal address is Lima, and the coordinate is inside Bath Township. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

**It is older than the county's government and its erection is on no record.** The 1885 compiler, working from the commissioners' books, found "no record of its establishment either in the records of Allen or Mercer County" — see [the place](../place/bath-township.yml). [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md).

**Its justices by 1831 were [Christopher Wood](../person/christopher-wood.yml), John Schrouf and James Daniels**, when Bath "had civil jurisdiction over nearly all Allen County" — which makes this government, not the county's, the first civil authority over most of this ground. [verified] — same source.

**Who governs it now.** Its trustees are Andrew F. Heffner and Brad A. Baxter, both to 31 December 2029, and Lisa R. Fillhart to 31 December 2027; its fiscal officer is Berlin Ralph Carroll II, whose term the roster runs to 31 March 2028 without giving its start. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

A district of 6,438 people over 52.909 square miles in the county's north, internal point 40.865493, -83.95681, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

6,281 of its people are in Allen County and 157 in Hancock — it reaches **out** across the county line, which the district-level tally this node was first written from could not see. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block. Its Allen County ground is 5,832 people of [Richland Township](../place/richland-township.yml) and 449 of [Monroe Township](../place/monroe-township.yml).

**It does not hold all of Bluffton.** 3,875 of the village's 3,967 people are in it and 92 are in the Cory-Rawson Local district, on the Hancock County side. [verified] — same source. It also holds [Beaverdam](../place/beaverdam.yml) and its 319 people, six miles south-west, which is the older fact this node was missing: the district is named for one village and serves two.

**Who governs it now.** Its five board members are Bradley James Dailey, Roni L. Kaufman and Wesley L. Klinger to 31 December 2029, and Alice Marie Basinger and Jeremy Patrick Scoles to 31 December 2027. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**It is the only district here that grew, and it is also the cheapest.** Enrolment rose 8.8 per cent between 2010 and 2023, from 1,107 to 1,204, in fourteen years during which the other eleven fell or stood still. It spends $10,839 a pupil, the lowest figure in the county, and its child poverty rate of 5.6 per cent is the lowest too. [verified] — [enrolment](../measure/allen-county-school-enrolment-2010-2023.yml), [the finance survey](../measure/allen-county-school-finance-2023.yml) and [child poverty](../measure/allen-county-school-district-poverty-2023.yml).

The municipal corporation governing [Delphos](../place/delphos.yml), the county's second city. **It is the only municipality here made by merger**: the county records that Delphos was originally four towns — Howard, Section Ten, West Bredeick and East Bredeick — which combined into one in 1851. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), cities and villages page.

Its territory crosses the Allen–Van Wert county line, and its 7,117 people divide 3,935 in Allen and 3,182 in Van Wert. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population and [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md). It is therefore the second corporation in this corpus, after [the Village of Bluffton](village-of-bluffton.yml), whose ground is not contained by one county — and unlike Bluffton, whose village is split between two school districts, this city's schools follow the corporation across the line entire.

**The corporation dates from an act of February 7, 1851.** Its first election was held March 3 of that year and returned Lester Bliss as mayor, Smith Talbott as recorder and five councilmen; F. J. Lye as treasurer and E. N. Talbott as marshal were elected on March 21. The corporation spent $80.67 in its first year. [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md), both scans carrying the act's date. So 1851 is not only the year four settlements became one settlement — it is the year they became one corporation, by a single act, and the merger and the incorporation are the same event.

**Who governs it now, as far as an Allen County source can see.** Andre Patrick McConnahea is mayor, Adam J. Kayser auditor and Andrew D. Knueve (R) director of law, all to 31 December 2027; Barbara J. Mesker (R) is treasurer to 31 December 2029. Mark Clement is president of council by appointment. Its three at-large council members are Michael J. Edelbrock (D) and, by appointment, Josh Bayliff and Scott Wiltsie. Michel A. Clement holds the 1st ward seat and Randy J. McElroy the 2nd, both by appointment. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**Five of these ten seats are held by appointees, and the ten are not the whole government.** This roster is a county's roster, and 3,182 of the city's 7,117 people live in Van Wert County: a ward seat is voted on inside its ward, so any ward of this city lying west of the line is invisible here. The corpus does not read these ten as the council of Delphos. [inference] Compare [Bluffton](village-of-bluffton.yml), whose council is elected at large and therefore appears whole in an Allen County roster despite the same kind of split. [verified] — [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml).

The municipal corporation governing [Lima](../place/lima.yml). Under Ohio law a municipality becomes a city rather than a village when its population passes 5,000, and it may adopt a home-rule charter; Lima has long been past that threshold. [inference]

**The corporation was created on March 29, 1842, and the town is eleven years older.** Lima was platted in 1831 and for its first decade had no government of its own — the original town "was entirely controlled by the county commissioners". In 1841 the inhabitants petitioned the commissioners for a system of village government; the village was established, and the town was organized on March 29, 1842 with H. D. V. Williams as mayor, W. McHenry as recorder, and five trustees. [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md). The county seat was thus a creature of the county board for eleven years before it was a corporation, which is the sharpest case in the corpus of why [the place](../place/lima.yml) and this node are separate things.

**Its territory demonstrably moved, and the corpus can now name when.** Between the 1980 and 1990 censuses Lima annexed ground from American, Bath and Shawnee townships; Bluffton village and Delphos city annexed in the same interval. [verified] — [1990 Census, Population and Housing Unit Counts, Ohio](../../catalog/census-cph-2-37-ohio.md), Geographic Change Notes. That is the first annexation event this corpus has ever held, and it converts the caveat below from a reasonable worry into a documented fact for one decade. [inference] The city's count fell from 47,827 to 45,549 across that decade **while the corporation was getting larger**.

**Who governs it now.** [Sharetta T. Smith](../person/sharetta-t-smith.yml) is mayor, on a term running 1 December 2025 to 30 November 2029. Randall S. Bartels is auditor and Anthony Layton Geiger director of law, both to 31 December 2029; Jamie Lamar Dixon Jr. is president of council to 2 January 2028. Its seven ward council members are Todd Gordon (1st), Jesse James Lowe II (3rd), Thomas Michael Wa Jones (5th) and Jonathan M. Neeper (7th) to 6 January 2030, and Anthony C. Wilkerson (2nd), Jeannine M. Jordan (4th) and Derry L. Glenn (6th) to 2 January 2028. Jordan was appointed and is the only appointee among the city's eleven seats. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**The term dates are evidence about the open question above.** This mayor's term year runs from 1 December, the council's terms turn on 5 January and 2 January, and [Delphos](city-of-delphos.yml) — the other city in the county — runs every one of its offices from 1 January to 31 December. Two cities in one county keeping different calendars is the kind of difference a charter makes and a statutory form does not. [inference]

A Putnam County district that reaches into Allen — 5,120 people over 73.137 square miles, internal point 40.907866, -84.118198, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

4,631 of its people are in Putnam County and 489 in Allen — 9.6 per cent. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block. The Allen County portion is 44 blocks in the north of [Monroe Township](../place/monroe-township.yml) and contains no incorporated place.

**Its board is not on Allen County's roster, and the reason is the same as Delphos's wards.** A school board is elected by the voters of its district, and this district's centre is in Putnam County, so no Allen County precinct votes on it. Nine of the twelve districts here have boards this corpus can name and three do not. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

756 pupils in 2023 against 896 in 2010, a fall of 15.6 per cent; $15,384 of current spending a pupil, which is the fourth-highest figure in the county on its fourth-smallest roll; 8.0 per cent child poverty. [verified] — [enrolment](../measure/allen-county-school-enrolment-2010-2023.yml), [the finance survey](../measure/allen-county-school-finance-2023.yml) and [child poverty](../measure/allen-county-school-district-poverty-2023.yml).

A district of 9,903 people over 53.041 square miles on the county's western edge, internal point 40.829646, -84.35015, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

**It is a Van Wert County district as much as an Allen County one.** 5,696 of its people are in Allen County and 4,207 in Van Wert — 57 per cent against 43. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block. Its Allen County ground is 5,547 people of [Marion Township](../place/marion-township.yml) and 149 of [Spencer Township](../place/spencer-township.yml).

It holds the whole of [Delphos](../place/delphos.yml) — all 7,117 people on both sides of the county line, in one district. [verified] — same source. That is the fact worth keeping: the city is split between two counties and its schools are not. Where a municipal boundary and a county boundary disagree, the school district followed the municipality.

**Who governs it now.** Its five board members are Matthew Richard Weitzel (R), Rebecca Suever and Wesley Aaron Ditto to 31 December 2029, and Karen Kay Grothouse and Lynn M. Bockey to 31 December 2027; Weitzel and Suever were appointed. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**It lost a fifth of its pupils**, 1,113 to 888 between 2010 and 2023 — very nearly [Lima](lima-city-school-district.yml)'s rate of loss, in a district a quarter the size. [verified] — [enrolment](../measure/allen-county-school-enrolment-2010-2023.yml). It spends $12,539 a pupil on 58.7 per cent local revenue — the second-highest local share in the county — and 10.6 per cent child poverty. [verified] — [the finance survey](../measure/allen-county-school-finance-2023.yml) and [child poverty](../measure/allen-county-school-district-poverty-2023.yml).

The county's second most populous school district — 18,876 people over 67.454 square miles, internal point 40.804278, -84.199108, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

It lies wholly inside Allen County and covers **five of the county's thirteen civil subdivisions**: 11,390 people in [American Township](../place/american-township.yml), 4,849 in [Lima](../place/lima.yml), all 1,231 in [Sugar Creek Township](../place/sugar-creek-township.yml), 1,082 in [Marion Township](../place/marion-township.yml) and 324 in [Amanda Township](../place/amanda-township.yml). [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block.

**Who governs it now.** Its five board members are Aaron J. Cunningham, Aundrea Kay Fricke and Benjamin Matthew Troyer to 31 December 2029, and Jaired Reginald Birks and Jeffrey L. Point to 31 December 2027. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**It is the county's second-largest district and its second-poorest.** 2,183 pupils, $13,472 a pupil, 51.3 per cent of revenue local, and 17.1 per cent of its children in poverty — nowhere near [Lima](lima-city-school-district.yml)'s 31.7 and twice [Shawnee](shawnee-local-school-district.yml)'s 8.8. [verified] — [enrolment](../measure/allen-county-school-enrolment-2010-2023.yml), [the finance survey](../measure/allen-county-school-finance-2023.yml) and [child poverty](../measure/allen-county-school-district-poverty-2023.yml). Enrolment fell 6.9 per cent from 2010.

blocks.text: The township government whose territory is [Jackson Township](../place/jackson-township.yml). Its township house is at 225 Sugar Street, Lafayette, its telephone is 419.649.6482, and its trustees meet on the first and third Tuesday of the month at 7:00 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

What the address file does carry is a fire department shared with the village: `LAFAYETTE & JACKSON TOWNSHIP FIRE DEPARTMENT IN LAFAYETTE AT 215 E SUGAR`, two doors from the township house address. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md). Jackson is one of only two townships in the county lying entirely inside one school district; the other is Sugar Creek.

**Erected June 6, 1831, on the first petition the Allen County commissioners ever granted** — see [the place](../place/jackson-township.yml). Re-formed as a congressional township in December 1834 after Auglaize, Perry and Bath had claimed sections back. [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md).
**William Watt, William Reese and Thomas Nash were the first trustees**, John Jamieson the first justice of the peace and Joseph Hall the first clerk. [verified] — same source.

**Who governs it now.** Its trustees are Christopher L. Shafer and Michael Wayne Bassitt, both to 31 December 2029, and James I. Shilling to 31 December 2027; its fiscal officer is Brandt C. Miller, to 31 March 2028. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**This township and the village inside it are administered from the same address.** The roster gives 225 E. Sugar Street, Lafayette for both this government and [the village of Lafayette](village-of-lafayette.yml). [verified] — same source. All four township officers were elected; four of the village's six council members were appointed. Two governments in one building, staffed in opposite ways. [verified] — [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml).

nodes.label: Lima City School District

blocks.text: The county's largest school district by population and its smallest by area — 28,122 people over 8.745 square miles, internal point 40.739641, -84.112076, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population. At 3,200 people to the square mile it is more than seven times as dense as any other district touching the county; the next is Shawnee Local at 417.

**It is not the city, and the gap runs both ways.** It holds 27,821 of Lima's 35,579 people — 78 per cent — while the other 7,758 residents of the city are in four suburban districts. It also reaches outside the corporate boundary: 301 people in [American Township](../place/american-township.yml), and unpopulated blocks in Shawnee and Bath townships that are the trace of annexed ground the school boundary followed. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block. The earlier form of this node said the boundary "does not follow the municipal or township lines around it. [inference] — from the area and internal point alone". It has now been compared against the places, and the inference holds in detail.

**Who governs it now.** Its five board members are Heather J. Rutz and Sandra Jean Monfort to 31 December 2029, and Alice Marie Donahue, Grant M. Sullivan and Saul E. Allen Jr. to 31 December 2027 — five elected seats on four-year terms, staggered two and three. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md). Five is the most the statute allows a city district under fifty thousand people, which is *"not less than three nor more than five members elected at large"*. [verified] — [Ohio Revised Code 3313.02](../../catalog/ohio-revised-code.md).

**It is the county's largest district, its poorest, its highest spender and the one that raises the least of what it spends.** 3,394 pupils in 2023, down from 4,280 in 2010; $19,321 of current spending a pupil; 18.4 per cent of revenue local against 59.2 from the state and 22.4 federal; 31.7 per cent of its children aged 5 to 17 in poverty. [verified] — [enrolment](../measure/allen-county-school-enrolment-2010-2023.yml), [the finance survey](../measure/allen-county-school-finance-2023.yml) and [child poverty](../measure/allen-county-school-district-poverty-2023.yml). Its property tax raises $3,098 a pupil where [Shawnee](shawnee-local-school-district.yml) raises $7,727.

**It lost a fifth of its pupils in thirteen years** — 886 of 4,280, against a county that fell under four per cent over the same span. [verified] — same sources. This district empties faster than the city it is named for. [inference]

refusals: The earlier form of this node said the boundary "does not follow the municipal or township lines around it.

properties.authority_source: Ohio Revised Code §1901.02, which names this court and fixes its territory as Allen County. [verified]

blocks.text: **Its name says Lima and its territory is the county.** "The Lima municipal court has jurisdiction within Allen county." [verified] — [Ohio Revised Code §1901.02](../../catalog/ohio-revised-code.md), quoted verbatim. The general rule in the same section is that municipal courts "have jurisdiction within the corporate limits of their respective municipal corporations"; Lima is one of the named exceptions, and the exception is the whole county. [verified] — same source.

**A second source agrees without saying so.** Its two judges appear on the roster of *Allen County's* elected officials rather than Lima's, which is where they would appear if the court's electorate were the city. [verified] — [Ohio county elected officials lookup](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md). [inference] — a court's judges are elected by the electors of its territory, so a countywide electorate implies a countywide territory.

**Two judges sit, on six-year terms**, which is the same length the [common pleas](allen-county-court-of-common-pleas.yml) judges serve and half again the four years every elected administrative officer of the county serves. [verified] — same roster. See [the office](../office/judge-of-the-lima-municipal-court.yml).

properties.authority_source: Order of the Allen County commissioners on a settlers' petition, setting it off from the north end of Amanda; recomposed February 28, 1848. [verified]

blocks.text: The township government whose territory is [Marion Township](../place/marion-township.yml). Its township house is at 5405 Kiggins Road, its telephone is 419.692.8846, and its trustees meet on the second and fourth Monday of the month at 7:00 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.814513, -84.319250, landmarked `MARION TOWNSHIP ROAD & POLICE DEPT`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

**It has its own police force.** The county's address file landmarks the building at the township house address as `MARION TOWNSHIP ROAD & POLICE DEPT`. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md). Three of the twelve townships here run police departments; the other nine are policed by the county sheriff.

**Set off from the north end of Amanda in December 1833** by the Allen County commissioners, and recomposed in the [reorganization of 1848](../event/reorganization-of-1848.yml) — see [the place](../place/marion-township.yml). [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md).

**Its first trustees after the 1848 change were Christian Stukey, Michael Swisher and Thomas J. Fair**, with William J. Cochran clerk and Ferdinand Miller treasurer; William Brady and William Scott were named road commissioners to open the Auglaize & Van Wert road. [verified] — same source.

**Who governs it now.** Its trustees are Gary V. Mack and Howard G. Violet, both to 31 December 2029, and Jerry Alan Gilden to 31 December 2027; its fiscal officer is Robert C. Kimmet, to 31 March 2028. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**This is the one township the corpus could already have named and did not.** The roster is indexed by precinct, and the single page it was first read from — precinct 0004 — is in this township, so these four officers were on the page the whole time and were passed over as local detail. The other eleven townships needed eighty-seven more pages. [verified] — same source.

properties.authority_source: Petition granted by the commissioners of Putnam County; the territory was attached to Allen County in 1848 with its name and organization intact. [verified]

blocks.text: The township government whose territory is [Monroe Township](../place/monroe-township.yml). Its township house is at 8500 Slabtown Road, its telephone is 419.641.5430, and its trustees meet on the second and fourth Monday of the month at 7:00 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.861214, -84.051203, landmarked `MONROE TOWNSHIP HOUSE`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

**Its township house has a Putnam County postal address.** The county gives it as `8500 Slabtown Road, Columbus Grove, Ohio 45833`, and Columbus Grove is a village in Putnam County. The building's coordinate is inside Monroe Township, in Allen County, and its `MUNI` is blank. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

**Organized in 1835 as a township of Putnam County**, and not in Allen County until the [reorganization of 1848](../event/reorganization-of-1848.yml), which let it keep both its name and its organization — see [the place](../place/monroe-township.yml). [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md).

**John Peters, Peter Harpster and Anthony Early were its first trustees**, with Benjamin Parker clerk and Luke Tipton justice of the peace. N. G. Kidd was still its clerk fifty years later. [verified] — same source.

**Who governs it now.** Its trustees are Aaron Patrick Vorst and Mark E. Diller, both to 31 December 2029, and Jon E. Basinger, whose term the roster runs to 31 December 2027 without giving its start; its fiscal officer is Amy S. Stechschulte, to 31 March 2028. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**All four were elected, and the village inside this township elected one officer of seven.** [Cairo](village-of-cairo.yml)'s mayor was elected; its six council seats are five appointees and a vacancy, with no elected member sitting. [verified] — [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml). The same 508 people are governed by a board they filled and a council they did not. [inference]

A Putnam County district whose southern edge crosses into Allen — 3,502 people over 67.625 square miles, internal point 41.000054, -83.948062, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

3,463 of its people are in Putnam County and **39 in Allen**, across seven blocks in the north of [Richland Township](../place/richland-township.yml). [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block.

**Its board is not on Allen County's roster.** A school board is elected by its own district's voters, and this district's centre is in Putnam County, so no Allen precinct votes on it. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

521 pupils, the second-smallest district holding ground here, at $15,610 of current spending a pupil — the third-highest figure in the county, on 6.6 per cent child poverty. [verified] — [enrolment](../measure/allen-county-school-enrolment-2010-2023.yml), [the finance survey](../measure/allen-county-school-finance-2023.yml) and [child poverty](../measure/allen-county-school-district-poverty-2023.yml). Cost per pupil here is a fact about size and not about need. [inference]

The smallest by population of the five districts lying wholly inside Allen County — 3,660 people over 33.598 square miles south-east of Lima, internal point 40.675113, -84.041425, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

**It contains no incorporated place and it is not rural.** 3,357 of its people are the whole of [Perry Township](../place/perry-township.yml) less 25, and the remaining 303 live inside the city of [Lima](../place/lima.yml). [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block. Those 303 are the smallest of the five slices Lima is cut into, and they are the reason this district is in the corpus as more than a name: a district with no village of its own still reaches into the county seat.

**Who governs it now.** Its five board members are Luke M. Taviano and Marc Alan Sidener to 31 December 2029, and Natalie Marie Scott, Thomas G. Ewing and Troy Patrick Cox to 31 December 2027; Scott was appointed. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**It has the county's second-highest child poverty rate.** 22.1 per cent of 602 children, against 31.7 in [Lima](lima-city-school-district.yml) and 8.8 in [Shawnee](shawnee-local-school-district.yml). [verified] — [child poverty](../measure/allen-county-school-district-poverty-2023.yml). 723 pupils, $13,791 a pupil, 48.2 per cent local revenue. [verified] — [enrolment](../measure/allen-county-school-enrolment-2010-2023.yml) and [the finance survey](../measure/allen-county-school-finance-2023.yml). The district and [Perry Township](../place/perry-township.yml) are not the same ground and this rate is not the township's. [inference]

properties.authority_source: Established by the county board in December 1833 and organized in April 1834 at Joseph Crossley's house. [verified]

blocks.text: The township government whose territory is [Perry Township](../place/perry-township.yml). Its township house is at 2408 E. Breese Road, its telephone is 419.221.2412, and its trustees meet on the first and third Tuesday of the month at 7:30 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.687591, -84.060925, landmarked `PERRY TOWNSHIP ADMINISTRATION BUILDING`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

It runs an administration building at the township house address and a police department a hundred yards east at 2501 E Breese Road. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md).

**Established by the county board in December 1833 and organized in April 1834** at the house of Joseph Crossley — see [the place](../place/perry-township.yml). [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md).

**Hugh Skilling Sr., John Ridenour and Joseph Crossley were elected trustees**, with Moses McDonald justice of the peace and James Chenoweth clerk — the man whose house it met in serving on its first board. [verified] — same source.

**Who governs it now.** Its trustees are Frank Eugene Clementz and Scott Stombaugh, both to 31 December 2029, and Kevin Walter Cox to 31 December 2027; its fiscal officer is Christina Rene Stombaugh, whose term the roster runs to 31 March 2028 without giving its start. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md). This corpus now names the board of this township twice, a hundred and ninety-two years apart: the three men elected at Joseph Crossley's house in 1834, and the three serving in 2026.

properties.authority_source: Authority granted by the commissioners of Putnam County on the petition of David Miller and others; the territory was attached to Allen County in 1848. [verified]

blocks.text: The township government whose territory is [Richland Township](../place/richland-township.yml). Its township house is at 8435 N. Dixie Highway, its telephone is 419.358.4897, and its trustees meet on the second and fourth Tuesday of the month at 8:00 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.862153, -83.934326, landmarked `RICHLAND TOWNSHIP GARAGE`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

The county's address file landmarks the building at that address as `RICHLAND TOWNSHIP GARAGE` and nothing else — the only one of the twelve whose sole landmark is a works building rather than a hall, house or administration office. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md).

**Organized in 1835 as a township of Putnam County**, on David Miller's petition, and not in Allen County until the [reorganization of 1848](../event/reorganization-of-1848.yml) — see [the place](../place/richland-township.yml). [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md).

**Henry Shank and Daniel Goble were its first justices of the peace and Henry Carter its first constable.** Carter's recollection, fifty years later, is the source for the township's name. [verified] — same source.

**Who governs it now.** Its trustees are Alan D. Myers and Seth C. Bixel, both to 31 December 2029, and Michael David Zimmerly to 31 December 2027; its fiscal officer is Lawrence Edward Hoffman, to 31 March 2028. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**Two villages sit on this township's ground and it is the only one of the three staffed entirely by election.** All four township officers were elected; three of the fourteen elective seats of [Bluffton](village-of-bluffton.yml) and [Beaverdam](village-of-beaverdam.yml) are held by appointees. [verified] — [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml).

The county's third largest district — 17,056 people over 40.932 square miles south and west of Lima, internal point 40.700628, -84.180974, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

It holds every one of [Shawnee Township](../place/shawnee-township.yml)'s 12,482 people, and more than a quarter of its own population lives elsewhere: 2,847 in [American Township](../place/american-township.yml), 1,033 inside [Lima](../place/lima.yml), 665 in [Amanda Township](../place/amanda-township.yml), and **29 across the line in Auglaize County**. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block. Those 29 people on four blocks are why this node no longer says its territory is within Allen County.
