It contains [Fort Shawnee](../place/fort-shawnee.yml) and its 6,263 people — a third of the district, in a place with no municipal government of its own. [verified] — same source. The earlier form of this node called the boundary's disagreement with the township lines an inference from area and internal point; the comparison has now been made against the places themselves.

**Who governs it now.** Its five board members are Manu B. Aggarwal, Marlena Franziska Schaaf and Scott R. Gephart to 31 December 2029, and Jerome J. O’Neal and Todd Joseph Washam to 31 December 2027; Aggarwal and Gephart were appointed. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**It raises more of its own money than any district in the county.** 65.8 per cent of its revenue is local and $7,727 a pupil comes from property tax — the highest figure in the county, against $3,098 in [Lima](lima-city-school-district.yml). [verified] — [the finance survey](../measure/allen-county-school-finance-2023.yml). It spends $13,260 a pupil, which is less than Lima does. Its child poverty rate is 8.8 per cent. [verified] — [child poverty](../measure/allen-county-school-district-poverty-2023.yml).

**Its enrolment fell 8.3 per cent between 2010 and 2023**, from 2,496 to 2,289 — a smaller fall than the twelve districts' 10.4 per cent. [verified] — [enrolment](../measure/allen-county-school-enrolment-2010-2023.yml).

properties.authority_source: Petition of the people of Shawnee granted by the Allen County commissioners in session, setting Township 4, Range 6 off from the Hog Creek Reservation. [verified]

blocks.text: The township government whose territory is [Shawnee Township](../place/shawnee-township.yml). Its township house is at 2530 Ft. Amanda Road, its telephone is 419.991.8706, and its trustees meet on the second and fourth Monday of the month at 10:00 a.m. — the only board in the county that meets in the morning. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

**No municipality shares its ground.** Its territory holds 12,482 people — the county's second most populous civil subdivision — and contains no incorporated place at all, so everything a village government would do here is done by this board. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population. The county's address file landmarks four separate township buildings at or beside 2530 Ft. Amanda Road — administration, police, road department and fire — which no other township here approaches. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md).

Ohio townships are governed by a three-member board of trustees and a fiscal officer, all elected. [inference] The county's site does not say so; it says only that trustees meet, which is the part this corpus can cite. That was the reasoning, and it is left standing here because the paragraph below is what replaced it.

**Set off December 1, 1834 from the Hog Creek Reservation**, on the petition of the people of Shawnee and "under the name of its original inhabitants" — see [the place](../place/shawnee-township.yml). [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md).

**It organized on December 13, 1834 in Ezekiel Hover's log house, with a list of twelve voters**: Griffith Breese, Joseph Hover and Benjamin Reed elected trustees and Ezekiel Hover clerk. Twelve voters then; 12,490 people now, and still no municipality. [verified] — same source.

**Who governs it now.** Its trustees are Kenneth James Gross and Paul E. Neff, both to 31 December 2029, and Arthur Joseph Recker Jr. to 31 December 2027; its fiscal officer is Kevin Dean Cooley, to 31 March 2028. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**The inference above is now a verified fact, and it holds for all twelve.** Every township in this county has three trustees and one fiscal officer, each on a four-year term, with two trustee seats standing for election in one odd year and the third two years later — and the fiscal officer's term year begins on 1 April where every trustee's begins on 1 January. [verified] — same source. The corpus reasoned the shape from Ohio practice and can now read it off the seats.

properties.authority_source: The commissioners' reorganization of February 28, 1848, out of the north-east quarter of Salem and the east half of Jennings, taken from Van Wert County. [verified]

blocks.text: The township government whose territory is [Spencer Township](../place/spencer-township.yml). Its township house is at 13080 Kolter Road, its telephone is 419.647.6172, and its trustees meet on the first Tuesday of the month at 7:30 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.699764, -84.354338, landmarked `SPENCER TOWNSHIP HALL`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

**Its trustees meet once a month**, where every other board in the county meets twice. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page. Nothing retrieved explains why, and it is not a matter of size: Spencer holds 3,067 people, more than four of the townships that meet twice.

The county's address file landmarks the building as `SPENCER TOWNSHIP HALL` and four separate township parks on Wisher Drive and Kolter Road — more park landmarks than any other township in the county. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md).

**The county's youngest township government, created February 28, 1848** out of Van Wert territory — see [the place](../place/spencer-township.yml). [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md).

**Charles C. Marshall was justice of the peace at organization**, and with Sebastian Lye and J. Hockenberry was elected trustee; Abram Huff was clerk and Sol. Wyatt, M.D., treasurer. [verified] — same source.

**Who governs it now.** Its trustees are Allen L. McMichael and Ron Eugene Leffel, both to 31 December 2029, and Ricky W. Keller to 31 December 2027; its fiscal officer is Kathleen Ann Keller, to 31 March 2028. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**The board that meets once a month elected all four of its officers.** [Spencerville](village-of-spencerville.yml), inside this township and holding most of its people, appointed four of its seven. [verified] — [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml). The township form and the village form are staffed in opposite ways on the same ground here, which is the clearest case of it in the county. [inference]

**The largest of the twelve by area** — 5,164 people over 89.368 square miles in the county's south-west, internal point 40.710853, -84.365128, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population. Fifty-eight people to the square mile: thinner than every district centred in this county, and thicker only than the two that reach it from Putnam and Auglaize by 39 people and 17.

It reaches into three counties: 3,990 people in Allen, 662 in Auglaize and 512 in Van Wert. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block. Its Allen County ground is 2,918 people of [Spencer Township](../place/spencer-township.yml) and 1,072 of [Amanda Township](../place/amanda-township.yml).

It holds [Spencerville](../place/spencerville.yml) and its 2,198 people — two fifths of the district in one village, and the rest spread over eighty square miles of farmland. [verified] — same source.

**Who governs it now.** Its five board members are D. Clarke Prichard, Elizabeth J. Klaus and John Robert Core to 31 December 2029, and Ryan McMichael and Spencer R. Clum to 31 December 2027. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

926 pupils in 2023 against 947 in 2010, a fall of 2.2 per cent — the smallest in the county after Allen East's, in fourteen years when only Bluffton grew. It spends $13,662 a pupil on 41.5 per cent local revenue and 50.2 per cent state, with 11.1 per cent child poverty. [verified] — [enrolment](../measure/allen-county-school-enrolment-2010-2023.yml), [the finance survey](../measure/allen-county-school-finance-2023.yml) and [child poverty](../measure/allen-county-school-district-poverty-2023.yml).

properties.authority_source: Set off as a division of Putnam County; reconstituted February 28, 1848 from the old township's south half and German Township's north tier. [verified]

blocks.text: The township government whose territory is [Sugar Creek Township](../place/sugar-creek-township.yml). Its township house is at 4130 W. Lincoln Highway, its telephone is 419.642.7390, and its trustees meet on the first and last Tuesday of the month at 8:00 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.844333, -84.182793, landmarked `SUGAR CREEK TOWNSHIP TOWN HALL`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

Its township house is in [Gomer](../place/gomer.yml), the only township house in the county whose postal address is a place with no government of its own — a census designated place, so the address names a settlement and not a corporation. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

**Set off in 1831 as a division of Putnam County**, and recomposed in the [reorganization of 1848](../event/reorganization-of-1848.yml) from the old township's south half and German Township's north tier — see [the place](../place/sugar-creek-township.yml). [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md).
**James Porter, Daniel Gray and William Turner were its first trustees**, with Abram Sarber clerk, Benjamin Clevenger treasurer and Obed Martin justice of the peace. [verified] — same source.

**Who governs it now.** Its trustees are Robert Brian Overholt and Willard R. Watkins, both to 31 December 2029, and William W. Williams to 31 December 2027; its fiscal officer is Jessica Lynn Cruikshank, to 31 March 2028. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md). The county's smallest township fills the same four seats as its largest. [verified] — [the race table](../measure/allen-county-race-2023.yml) for both populations: one officer for every 350 people here and one for every 3,600 in [American Township](american-township.yml), computed from those. [inference]

nodes.label: Ohio Third District Court of Appeals

blocks.text: **The only jurisdiction in this corpus larger than the county, and it is seated inside it.** The Third District hears appeals from seventeen Ohio counties — Allen, Auglaize, Crawford, Defiance, Hancock, Hardin, Henry, Logan, Marion, Mercer, Paulding, Putnam, Seneca, Shelby, Union, Van Wert and Wyandot — and its office is at 204 N. Main Street in Lima. [verified] — [the court's own site](../../catalog/third-district-court-of-appeals.md).

Every other jurisdiction here is the county or a piece of it. This one contains the county, which is why it is the first node to make [`covers`](allen-county-court-of-common-pleas.yml) point at ground the corpus does not otherwise describe: sixteen of its seventeen counties are outside this corpus entirely. [inference]

**Its records for this district are kept by a county officer.** The Allen County [clerk of courts](../office/allen-county-clerk-of-courts.yml) handles the filing and preservation of the Third District's documents alongside those of the county's own trial court. [verified] — [the clerk's site](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md). So an elected officer of one county keeps the record of a court serving seventeen. [inference]
**Four judges sit** — John R. Willamowski, William R. Zimmerman, Mark C. Miller and Juergen A. Waldick. [verified] — [the court's site](../../catalog/third-district-court-of-appeals.md).
Their terms all begin in February and no two expire in the same year. [verified] — same source.

refusals: **They had no nodes here for one phase, on a rule that did not survive its second case.** The rule was that this corpus writes a person where Allen County's *own* electors choose the officer; applied next to the county's state senator and state representative, it excluded those too, and a county reference that cannot say who represents the county in the legislature is not a reference.

properties.authority_source: Authority granted by the Allen County commissioners on May 13, 1878, on petition. [verified]

blocks.text: The municipal corporation governing [Beaverdam](../place/beaverdam.yml), **incorporated in 1878**, twenty-five years after the settlement it governs was established in 1853. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), cities and villages page.

It governs 319 people over 0.63 square miles, wholly inside Allen County and inside [Richland Township](../place/richland-township.yml). [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) and [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md).

**It was organized in 1878 under authority of the county commissioners, granted May 13 that year**, with Joseph Shull elected mayor and Albert Shull clerk; they served until 1881. [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md). The village had been platted twenty-five years earlier by **Frederick Shull** — so the men who took the corporation's first two offices carry the founder's surname.

**Who governs it now.** Todd Aaron Long is mayor to 31 December 2027. Its six council members are Anthony E. Myers and Carl L. Murray to 31 December 2027, and Jerry A. Neuenschwander, Thomas Joe Nowlan, Barbara Ann Gossard and Tyler James Powley to 31 December 2029; the last two were appointed. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

Two of seven is the second-lightest use of appointment among the county's seven villages, and this is the smallest of them. [verified] — [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml). Whichever way village seats come to be filled by appointment here, it is not a straightforward matter of size. [inference]

The municipal corporation governing [Bluffton](../place/bluffton.yml). Its territory crosses the Allen–Hancock county line, which makes it the corpus's worked case of a jurisdiction whose ground is not contained by one county. [verified] — the county-line crossing is recorded by the Census Bureau's `(pt.)` designation in [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md).

**Who governs it now.** Richard Lee Johnson (R) is mayor to 31 December 2027. Its six council members are Benjamin Lawrence Stahl and Joseph W. Sehlhorst to 31 December 2027, and Elizabeth A. Gordon Hancock, Phillip A. Talavinia, Thomas L. Downey and Robert Benjamin Hill (R) to 31 December 2029; Hill was appointed. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**The county's largest village is also the one that appoints least.** One of its seven elective seats is held by an appointee, against four of seven in Lafayette and in Spencerville, and all five seated members of Cairo's council. [verified] — [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml).

Its council is elected at large rather than by ward, which is why the Allen County roster carries all six seats of a village whose people are split between two counties: every voter in it votes on every seat. [inference] Compare [Delphos](city-of-delphos.yml), where the ward seats are county-scoped and the roster reaches only part of the council.

The municipal corporation governing [Cairo](../place/cairo.yml), 517 people over 0.277 square miles inside [Monroe Township](../place/monroe-township.yml). [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) and [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md).

It shares a fire and rescue service with the township it sits in, landmarked `CAIRO-MONROE TOWNSHIP VOLUNTEER FIRE & RESCUE`. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md).

**Who governs it now, and it is the sharpest case of appointment in the county.** John M. Vandemark is mayor to 31 December 2027, elected. Its six council seats are Bruce Jerome Painter and Gary M. Acheson to 31 December 2027, Bradley A. Clark, Jack Alan Arnold and Miles Lowell Bicknell to 31 December 2029, and one seat vacant — and all five sitting members are marked appointed. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md). **No elected member sits on this village's council.**

Its 508 people are governed by two boards: this one, and [Monroe Township](monroe-township.yml)'s, whose four officers were all elected. [verified] — [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml). The same electorate filled one government and not the other. [inference]

The municipal corporation governing [Elida](../place/elida.yml), **incorporated in 1878** — the same year as [Beaverdam](village-of-beaverdam.yml), twenty miles across the county — over a settlement established in 1852. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), cities and villages page.

**The mechanism is now known for Beaverdam and it is a county proceeding, not a state act.** Beaverdam was organized "under authority of the commissioners, granted May 13" 1878, and [Lafayette](village-of-lafayette.yml) the same way in 1867. [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md). This village's own incorporation is confirmed for 1878 by the same source, which names **R. R. Murray** as its first mayor, records his resignation that November, R. Rice appointed president in the interim and Dr. John Sherrick chosen mayor in February 1879 — and does not say by whose authority. [verified] — same source.

It governs 1,923 people over 1.102 square miles inside [American Township](../place/american-township.yml), and it is the only incorporated place in that township. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) and [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md).

**Who governs it now.** Darryl J. Nichols is mayor to 31 December 2027. Its six council members are John P. Heltman and Jon T. Jenkins to 31 December 2027, and Burlin L. Sherrick, Joseph G. Shehata, Kenneth Ray Hall and Michael W. Campbell to 31 December 2029; Heltman, Jenkins, Sherrick and Shehata were appointed. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

Four of the six council members were appointed, in the county's third-largest village and the only municipality in [American Township](american-township.yml) — whose own four officers were all elected. [verified] — [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml).

The municipal corporation governing [Harrod](../place/harrod.yml), 423 people over 0.234 square miles inside [Auglaize Township](../place/auglaize-township.yml). [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) and [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md).

The village was established in 1884 and is named for the Harrod family, who settled the ground in 1841 — forty-three years between the family and the village. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), cities and villages page. It is the only municipality in the county the source names a family for; the others are named for a feature, a place elsewhere, or nothing it says.

**Who governs it now, and most of it is nobody.** Mark Anthony Blake is mayor to 31 December 2027, appointed. Of six council seats, one running to 31 December 2027 is vacant and Cheryl Renee Rodriguez holds the other on that term by appointment; of the four running to 31 December 2029, Christine Jean Hennis Decker was elected and Harry P. Romell, Ritchie D. Frisby and Zachary Joseph Voisin were appointed. Its board of public affairs has three seats and all three are empty. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**One person in this village's government of ten seats was put there by its voters.** Four seats are vacant, five are held by appointees, and the tenth is a council member elected in 2025. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md), counted at [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml). No other government in the county is close to that.

The municipal corporation governing [Lafayette](../place/lafayette.yml), **incorporated in 1868** — the earliest incorporation date this corpus holds for any municipality in the county. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), cities and villages page.

It governs 406 people over 0.233 square miles inside [Jackson Township](../place/jackson-township.yml). Its corporate boundary is also, exactly, a voting precinct and nothing else: precinct `LAFAYETTE` holds every block of the village and no block outside it. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block geography. The village shares a fire department with the township, at an address two doors from the township house. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md).

**The commissioners granted authority to organize it on September 3, 1867**, on M. C. Murnagh's petition, and the first election was held March 13, 1868 — William Smith, William Maginnis and T. W. Corbett judges, James Fookes and S. Knoble clerks of election, Murnagh himself elected. [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md). The county's website gives "1868" and collapses two dates in different years.

**Who governs it now.** Jeffrey S. McVicker is mayor to 31 December 2027. Its six council members are Matthew Christophe Hager and Robert Lynn Hutchinson to 31 December 2027, and Adam W. Hawk, James Alan Wireman, Matthew Allan McKinley and Michael H. Hefner to 31 December 2029; Hutchinson, Hawk, Wireman and McKinley were appointed. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**This village and the township it sits in are run out of the same building**, 225 E. Sugar Street, and the two are staffed in opposite ways: [Jackson Township](jackson-township.yml) elected all four of its officers and four of this council's six were appointed. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md) and [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml).

properties.authority_source: An act of incorporation passed in 1867; the first village election followed the same year. [verified]

blocks.text: The municipal corporation governing [Spencerville](../place/spencerville.yml), 2,198 people over 0.965 square miles inside [Spencer Township](../place/spencer-township.yml) — the largest of the six villages lying wholly inside the county, though smaller than [Bluffton](../place/bluffton.yml), which does not. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) and [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md).

**It was founded on the canal.** The county records the settlement as founded in 1844 on the banks of the [Miami and Erie Canal](../site/miami-and-erie-canal.yml). [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), cities and villages page. That is the first thing in this corpus to connect the canal to a settlement that still exists: the canal node and [the canal era](../period/canal-era.yml) had until now no consequence anywhere else in the graph, and a village dated to the canal's own decade is one.

**The act of incorporation was passed in 1867 and the first village election held that year**, returning J. C. Campbell mayor, Merritt Harvey recorder, Jacob Dehart treasurer and W. H. Orcutt marshal, with five councilmen. [verified] — [History of Allen County, 1885](../../catalog/leeson-allen-county-1885.md), which then carries the roll of officers year by year to 1885. Twenty-three years separate the settlement from the corporation.

**Who governs it now, and the roll resumes after a hundred and forty-one years.** Darrell Edward Pugin is mayor to 31 December 2027. Its six council members are Anthony Joseph Lammers and Courtney Danielle Brown to 31 December 2027, and James E. Penix Jr. (R), Katie Ruth Cotterman (D), Nicholas Richard Goergens (R) and Nicole L. Lotz to 31 December 2029; all four of the 2029 seats were filled by appointment. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md). This corpus held the officers of this village for every year from 1867 to 1885 and for no year after; it now holds 1885 and 2026, and nothing between.

**Three of the four appointees carry a party letter**, which almost nothing else at this level of government in the county does — seven of the 145 seated township, village and school officers, and six of those seven are appointees. [verified] — [the seat count](../measure/allen-county-elected-seats-2026.yml).

An Auglaize County district with the thinnest reach into Allen of any of the twelve — 2,698 people over 62.864 square miles, internal point 40.591434, -83.964064, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

It is three counties wide and almost entirely in one: 2,629 people in Auglaize, 52 in Logan and **17 in Allen**, on two blocks at the south-east corner of [Auglaize Township](../place/auglaize-township.yml). [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block.

**Its board is not on Allen County's roster.** A school board is elected by its own district's voters, and this district's centre is in Auglaize County. [verified] — [the elected officials roster](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md).

**It is the smallest district holding ground in this county and the second-highest spender per pupil.** 472 pupils in 2023 against 590 in 2010 — a fall of 20.0 per cent, one of the three steepest here — at $17,896 a pupil on 10.2 per cent child poverty. [verified] — [enrolment](../measure/allen-county-school-enrolment-2010-2023.yml), [the finance survey](../measure/allen-county-school-finance-2023.yml) and [child poverty](../measure/allen-county-school-district-poverty-2023.yml).

nodes.label: Allen County age structure, 2023

properties.method: 2023 five-year estimates. Under-18 sums B01001 male 3-6 and female 27-30; 65-and-over sums male 20-25 and female 44-49. The twelve townships and Lima sum to the county's 101,685. [verified]
properties.parameter: median age (B01002) and population by age (B01001)

blocks.text: Median age and the shares under 18 and 65 or older, for the county, its thirteen civil subdivisions, the state and the nation. [verified] — [American Community Survey](../../catalog/census-acs-summary-file.md), 2023 five-year estimates.

**Lima is the young end of this county, not the old one.** Its median age is 35.4 against the county's 39.7, its 65-and-over share is 15.6 per cent against 18.7, and its under-18 share is higher than the county's. [verified] — same source. Eleven of the twelve townships are older than the city by the 65-and-over measure.

The corpus does not establish that. The city is younger than every part of the county except Sugar Creek and Spencer townships, so whatever natural decrease the county has is not principally Lima's, and the two findings do not compose into that story. [verified] — see [natural change](allen-county-natural-change-2021-2024.yml) and [the depopulation period](../period/depopulation.yml).
Sugar Creek Township's median age of 29.9 in 1,398 people is the shape a college makes in a small denominator, and this node does not read it as a finding about that township. [inference]

refusals: The corpus does not establish that.

properties.method: Census of Agriculture, harvested acreage and production for the 2022 calendar year, read from NASS's Quick Stats bulk county file. The 1909 column is the Thirteenth Census, enumerated April 15 1910 for the 1909 crop year. Yields are computed here by dividing production by harvested acres, which is not how either census reports yield and is comparable only because both report both terms. [inference] `(D)` is a suppressed cell, not a zero; a dash is a crop the source does not name for this county in that year, which for 1909 soybeans is a statement about the volume's crop list and not a count of zero acres. [verified]
properties.parameter: crop acreage and production, Allen County

blocks.text: What the county grows, beside what it grew in the year this corpus already measures. [verified] — [USDA Census of Agriculture](../../catalog/usda-census-of-agriculture.md), county file, and [Abstract of the Thirteenth Census](../../catalog/census-1910-abstract-supplement-ohio.md).

**The county's largest crop did not exist here in 1909.** Soybeans took 76,200 acres in 2022, more than corn, and the 1910 census names no soybean acreage in Allen County at all. [verified] — [the Census of Agriculture](../../catalog/usda-census-of-agriculture.md) and [the Thirteenth Census](../../catalog/census-1910-abstract-supplement-ohio.md).

**An acre of Allen County corn yields five times what it did**, 192.7 bushels against 38.7, and an acre of wheat six times, 81.8 against 13.4. [inference] — computed here by division. The county grew a quarter more corn acres in 2022 than in 1909 and took six and a quarter times the grain off them.

**The oats went with the horses.** 30,156 acres of oats in 1909, 11 acres on three operations in 2022; 3,107 acres of rye then, and now one operation in the county, whose acreage the census withholds because one operation is all there is. [verified] — same sources. Hay fell from 39,664 acres to 2,431. Together those three crops were 72,927 acres in 1909 — twenty-eight per cent of the county — and they were what fed the 14,676 horses and 21,336 cattle counted in [the same volume](allen-county-domestic-animals-1910.yml).

**Two crops are now 84.9 per cent of the harvest.** Soybeans and corn take 140,976 of the county's 165,982 cropland acres. [inference] — computed here. What is left is wheat, 2,686 acres of hay and haylage, 793 acres of popcorn on fourteen operations, and $1,663,000 of vegetables, fruit, nursery stock and everything else together. [verified] — [the 2022 county profile](../../catalog/usda-census-of-agriculture.md).

nodes.label: Allen County domestic animals, on farms and off, 1910

properties.method: Thirteenth Census of Agriculture, enumerated April 15, 1910. Read from rendered images of a 400-dpi scan. Checked by arithmetic self-closure: on the farms the seven animal values sum to the printed $2,501,226 exactly, and cattle, horses, mules, swine and sheep each sum from their own age and sex classes; off the farms the five values sum to $350,736 exactly. The colonies-of- bees value is damaged on this scan and was recovered as $2,561 from the property total, an identity that closes exactly in the neighbouring county column. County totals are added here. [inference]
properties.parameter: domestic animals on and off farms, Allen County

blocks.text: The county's animals counted twice over — once on the farms and once inside the town lots. [verified] — [Abstract of the Thirteenth Census, Supplement for Ohio](../../catalog/census-1910-abstract-supplement-ohio.md), statistics of agriculture, Table 1 (farms and ranges) and Table 6 (not on farms).

**There were 14,676 horses in Allen County in 1910 — one for every 3.9 people.** [inference] — computed from the two tables, against the county's 56,580. The horses were worth $1,391,032 on the farms and $304,989 off them, together more than half the value of every animal in the county.

**1,788 inclosures that were not farms kept animals**, holding 2,766 horses, 887 cattle and 664 swine. [verified] — same source, Table 6. This is the town half of the county: a place that was half city by population and nine-tenths farm by ground still moved itself on horses, and 713 of its dairy cows stood in yards rather than fields. See [Lima](../place/lima.yml) and [the farms](allen-county-farms-1900-1910.yml).
**The swine outnumbered the people.** [inference] — 59,695 against 56,580, computed here. Sheep and goats came to 41,240 and cattle to 21,336.

**There is a later count now, and it does not say when the horses went.** In 2022 the county held 316 horses and ponies, 8,576 cattle, 877 sheep and 622 goats, and a dairy herd the census will not print. [verified] — [the Census of Agriculture](../../catalog/usda-census-of-agriculture.md); see [the modern livestock](allen-county-livestock-2002-2022.yml). Every animal in the 1910 table is down by nine-tenths or more except the swine, which nearly quadrupled to 235,800.

refusals: So the fall from 14,676 happened somewhere in the ninety-two years between, and this corpus still cannot say when.

nodes.label: Allen County elective seats and how their holders arrived, 2026

properties.method: Union of the eighty-eight precinct pages of the boards of elections roster, deduplicated on the office name and the page's own `hid_office` code. Vacancies are counted from its `N Vacant Seat(s)` rows and appointments from its `*Appointed*` marker; the class column is this corpus's grouping and the roster totals nothing. [verified] **It is a county's roster, so a ward seat of a city that crosses the county line does not appear.** Delphos contributes ten seats here and 3,182 of its people live in Van Wert County, so its council is undercounted by an unknown number of ward seats. [inference] No other government here is affected: Bluffton also crosses a line and elects its council at large.
properties.parameter: seated holders of elective office, and seats vacant, by class of government

blocks.text: Every elective seat whose constituency lies inside Allen County, with the seat filled or vacant and — where filled — whether the roster marks its holder as appointed to it. [verified] — [the elected officials lookup](../../catalog/ohio-boe-elected-officials-allen.md), read across all eighty-eight precincts.

**Twenty-three per cent of this county's local government arrived by appointment.** Of the 166 seated township, village, city and school officers, 39 hold seats they were appointed to fill. [verified] — same source. Every one of the twenty-two county offices and judgeships is filled, and every one of them by election. [verified]

**The village form is where it concentrates, and size is not what separates it from the township form.** Twenty-five of the forty-seven seated village officers were appointed and five village seats stand empty, against one appointment and no vacancy across all forty-eight township seats. [verified] — same source. [Spencer Township](../jurisdiction/spencer-township.yml) holds 3,024 people and [Spencerville](../jurisdiction/village-of-spencerville.yml) inside it holds 2,164, so most of the township's people are the village's people and both govern them. [verified] — [the race table](allen-county-race-2023.yml) and [the estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), a year apart in vintage. The township fills four seats and elected all four; the village fills seven and appointed four of them. [verified]

**Two villages cannot fill their governments at all.** [Cairo](../jurisdiction/village-of-cairo.yml)'s six-member council is five appointees and one vacant seat: no elected member sits on it. [Harrod](../jurisdiction/village-of-harrod.yml)'s board of public affairs is three seats and all three are empty; of its ten village seats, four are vacant, five are held by appointees and one — a single council member — was elected. [verified] — same source.

refusals: This does not establish that these seats go unfilled because nobody stands for them.

nodes.label: Allen County employment by sector, 1986 and 2022

properties.method: County Business Patterns county files for 1986 and 2022, with sector 62 traced across 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015 and 2020. Both endpoint years close exactly: the ten 1986 SIC divisions sum to 45,917 and the twenty 2022 NAICS sectors to 42,814, each equal to its file's own total row. Government, the self-employed and farms are excluded. [verified]
properties.parameter: private employment by industry sector, Allen County

blocks.text: What the county's private workforce did, at the two ends of the only span this corpus can measure it over. [verified] — [County Business Patterns](../../catalog/census-county-business-patterns.md).

**Health care is the county's largest private employer sector, and manufacturing is second.** [verified] — same source. In 1986 manufacturing employed more people than the next two divisions together.

**The two schemes are not comparable line by line and the top line is the point.** SIC "services" in 1986 is a division that NAICS breaks across health care, accommodation, professional services and more, so the 1986 column cannot be subtracted from the 2022 one sector by sector. [verified] — the break is a change of definition. What survives the break is the rank of manufacturing: first in 1986, second in 2022. [inference]

**Health care did not simply rise past manufacturing, and this node had the shape of its fall wrong.** Sector 62 peaked at **12,431 in 2013** — not at the 11,744 of 2010 this node used to call its high — and stood above 11,744 again in 2016, before falling to 9,151 in 2022. [verified] — same source, read every year rather than every fifth; see [the annual series](allen-county-health-care-employment-2010-2022.yml) and [a sample is not a series](../../decisions/a-sample-is-not-a-series.yml). Against 2010 the county's largest sector still lost 2,593 while [manufacturing gained 1,446](allen-county-manufacturing-employment-1986-2022.yml). [inference]

**What contracted is now established, even though why is not.** Of the 2,593 lost since 2010, hospitals are 1,866, nursing and residential care 549, social assistance 170, and ambulatory care 8. [verified] — same source, read annually. The county's five hospitals are named, and their own reported full-time equivalents fell across the same span. See [hospital employment](allen-county-hospital-employment-2011-2023.yml).

nodes.label: Allen County farm output and farm expenses, 1909

properties.method: Thirteenth Census of Agriculture, for the calendar year 1909. Read from rendered images of a 400-dpi scan. Checked by arithmetic self-closure: the six crop-value classes sum to $2,425,973 exactly; the six cereals sum to the printed cereal acreage and to the printed bushel total; the six tame grasses sum to the tame-grass acreage and tonnage, and those plus three minor forages sum to the hay total — eight closures with no residual. The orchard and small-fruit itemisations leave residuals, as they do in the state column, because both omit minor kinds. [verified]
properties.parameter: value of crops, live stock products and farm expenses, Allen County

blocks.text: What the county's farms grew, sold and spent in the same year the corpus measures Lima's factories. [verified] — [Abstract of the Thirteenth Census, Supplement for Ohio](../../catalog/census-1910-abstract-supplement-ohio.md), statistics of agriculture, Tables 3, 4 and 5.

**Corn was half the county's cropland and two-thirds of its grain.** [verified] — same source. Cereals took 100,285 acres and yielded 3,146,354 bushels; corn alone was 51,293 of those acres. Wheat was a minor crop here, on a seventh of the cereal acreage. The county grew no tobacco and no sugar beets at all.

**Farms spent $184,390 in cash on labour in 1909**, with 1,571 of the 2,939 farms reporting any, plus $47,888 in rent and board furnished. [verified] — same source, Table 5. Fertilizer took $12,957 across 428 farms and feed $63,780 across 708. Receipts from the sale of feedable crops were $423,118.

**Against this, Lima's factories made $7,753,877 of products in the same year.** [verified] — [Lima manufactures](lima-manufactures-1899-1909.yml), from the manufactures chapter of this same volume. [inference] Both are gross output and neither nets out what was bought to make it, so the ratio of about three to one is a comparison of two gross figures and not of two incomes.

nodes.label: Allen County farms and farm property, 1900–1910

properties.method: Thirteenth Census of Agriculture, enumerated April 15, 1910, with 1900 comparatives printed in italics. Read from rendered images of a 400-dpi scan. Checked by arithmetic self-closure: the three tenure classes of Table 2 sum to Table 1's farm count, acreage, improved acreage and land-and-buildings value independently; the ten size classes sum to 2,939; improved plus woodland plus other unimproved sums to land in farms; the four property components sum to the total in both years; and all six printed averages and percentages recompute. [verified]
properties.parameter: farms, farm acreage and value of farm property, Allen County

blocks.text: What the county was made of, on the ground, at the height of the oil boom. [verified] — [Abstract of the Thirteenth Census, Supplement for Ohio](../../catalog/census-1910-abstract-supplement-ohio.md), statistics of agriculture, Tables 1 and 2.

**Nine-tenths of Allen County was farmland in 1910 — 240,472 acres of 259,840, or 92.5 per cent.** [verified] — same source, which prints the percentage and the land area beside it. Of that, 203,222 acres were improved, 32,316 were woodland in farms and 4,934 were otherwise unimproved. The average farm was 81.8 acres; the commonest was between 50 and 99 acres, and 1,138 of the 2,939 were that size. One farm in the county exceeded 500 acres and none reached 1,000.

**The county had 2,939 farms in 1910 and 2,858 in 1900, on 240,472 acres against 245,283.** [verified] — same source. Farms rose by 81 and farmland fell by 4,811 acres, about 2 per cent, while improved acreage *rose* by 6,757. Twenty-five years after [the strike](../event/lima-oil-strike.yml), whatever the boom did to this county, it had not taken the farms out of it. See [Lima manufactures](lima-manufactures-1899-1909.yml) for the other side of the same volume, and [what the county was](../period/lima-oil-boom.yml).

**The farms that multiplied were rented ones.** Owner-operated farms fell from 2,089 to 2,046 while tenanted farms rose from 730 to 871, and tenancy went from 25.5 to 29.6 per cent of all farms. [verified] — same source, Table 2. Of the 871 tenants, 509 paid shares and 275 paid cash. Of 2,046 owners, 655 carried mortgage debt and 1,378 were free of it.

**The other end of the century is measured now.** 178,921 acres in 2022, 69.4 per cent of the county, with 94,325 of those acres rented from somebody else. [verified] — [the Census of Agriculture](../../catalog/usda-census-of-agriculture.md); see [the modern series](allen-county-farms-2002-2022.yml). The 2,939 farms of 1910 and the 897 of 2022 are not subtracted here: the two censuses use different definitions of a farm, and the difference between the thresholds is not a quantity anything in this corpus can supply. See [a farm count is a definition](../../decisions/a-farm-count-is-a-definition.yml).

nodes.label: Allen County farms, farmland and farm income, 2002–2022

properties.method: Census of Agriculture, taken for the 2022 calendar year, read from NASS's Quick Stats bulk county file and checked against the published county profile, which agrees on every headline figure. The four tenure rows sum to land in farms exactly and the two sales components sum to the total exactly. NASS defines a farm as "any place from which $1,000 or more of agricultural products were produced and sold, or normally would have been sold, during the census year", which is not the definition the 1910 census used. [verified] See [a farm count is a definition](../../decisions/a-farm-count-is-a-definition.yml).
properties.parameter: farms, land in farms and value of products sold, Allen County

blocks.text: Five agricultural censuses of the county's largest land use, and the first this corpus has read since 1910. [verified] — [USDA Census of Agriculture](../../catalog/usda-census-of-agriculture.md), county files.

**Allen County was 92.5 per cent farmland in 1910 and is 69.4 per cent farmland now** — 178,921 acres of the 257,629 in its 402.545 square miles. [inference] — computed here from [the 1910 farms](allen-county-farms-1900-1910.yml) and [the county's land area](allen-county-land-area-2020.yml). The two censuses measure land area on different geographies, so the shares are firmer than the difference between them.

**Nine-tenths of the fall happened before this series begins.** Land in farms was 240,472 acres in 1910 and 188,150 in 2002 — 52,322 acres gone — against 9,229 more across the twenty years since. [inference] — same two sources. There is no agricultural census between them in this catalog, so this corpus knows that the farmland went and cannot say when. See [when the farmland went](../question/when-the-farmland-went.yml).

**Land in farms, five censuses in one line.** 188,150 acres in 2002, 187,238 in 2007, 183,186 in 2012, 186,623 in 2017 and 178,921 in 2022, against 240,472 in 1910. [verified] — same source, and [the 1910 farms](allen-county-farms-1900-1910.yml).

**More than half the county's farmland is worked by someone who does not own it.** 94,325 of 178,921 acres are rented — 90,661 by 268 part-owner operations and 3,664 by 38 tenants — and the 591 operations that own everything they farm hold 34,912 acres between them, a fifth of the total. [verified] — same source, tenure domain, whose four figures close on the county acreage exactly.

**So 268 operations farm 78.4 per cent of the ground.** [inference] — computed here. In 1910 the same county held 2,939 farms, of which 2,046 were owner-operated. [verified] — [the 1910 farms](allen-county-farms-1900-1910.yml).

**The census cannot resolve its own headline.** The county profile prints farms up 5 per cent and land in farms down 4 per cent since 2017; the figures are 897 ± 69 farms and 178,921 ± 16,171 acres, so the first change is inside one standard error and the second is inside half of one. [verified] — same source, Appendix A Table C. **39.0 per cent of the county's farm count is adjustment for coverage, nonresponse and misclassification rather than a returned form**, and 28.6 per cent of its acreage is. The corpus does not read the sales row of that table, whose standard error is printed in a unit the table does not name.

**Federal money reached 344 of the 897.** $1,898,000 in 2022, of which $698,000 went to 283 operations for conservation and wetlands and $1,200,000 to 86 for everything else. [verified] — same source. Expenses were $168,593,000 against $240,849,000 of sales; feed alone was $34,822,000, a fifth of all spending, in a county whose animals are described [next door](allen-county-livestock-2002-2022.yml).

refusals: There is no agricultural census between them in this catalog, so this corpus knows that the farmland went and cannot say when.

properties.method: Summed by candidate over the county's 88 precincts, from a volunteer transcription of the certified returns. [verified]
properties.parameter: votes cast for governor

blocks.text: Of 35,961 votes for governor, **24,200 for DeWine and 10,825 for Cordray** — 67.3 per cent against 30.1, with 605 for Irvine and 331 for Gadell-Newton. [verified] — [OpenElections](../../catalog/openelections-ohio.md), summed over the county's 88 precincts.

It sits between the two presidential elections in this corpus at 66.5 and 69.0 per cent Republican, which is the useful thing about it: the county's partisan balance barely moved between a presidential year and a midterm, while **the number of people voting fell by a fifth** — 45,815 in 2016 to 35,961 here, and back to 47,993 in 2020. [verified] — same source, and [2016](allen-county-presidential-vote-2016.yml) and [2020](allen-county-presidential-vote-2020.yml).
Who turns out changes far more here than how they vote. [inference] — from three elections, which is enough to see the pattern and not enough to date it.

nodes.label: Allen County health care employment by subsector, 2010–2022

properties.method: County files, fipstate 39 fipscty 003. The four subsectors sum to the sector total exactly in all thirteen years, so no line is suppressed. [verified]
properties.parameter: paid employees for pay period including March 12, NAICS 62 and its four subsectors

blocks.text: The county's largest private sector, every year rather than every fifth. [verified] — [County Business Patterns](../../catalog/census-county-business-patterns.md).

**The sector peaked at 12,431 in 2013, in a year nobody had looked at**, and hospitals are where the fall since went: 1,866 of the 2,593 lost from 2010, 1,049 of the 3,280 lost from the 2013 peak. [verified] — same source. Which share depends on the baseline, and all three are in [a sample is not a series](../../decisions/a-sample-is-not-a-series.yml).

refusals: This does not establish why any of it fell.

nodes.label: Allen County mortgage lending, 2018-2024

properties.method: Rates use actions 1, 2 and 3 and exclude withdrawn, purchased and incomplete files, as in [the single year](allen-county-home-lending-2023.yml). [verified] "Lima tracts" is the same sixteen of thirty-five used there. Dollar totals are sums of published loan amounts, each rounded to a $10,000 midpoint, so a total of this size carries a rounding band of its own and is quoted to the nearest hundred thousand. [inference]
properties.parameter: mortgage applications acted on, originations, denials and dollars originated
properties.unit: applications acted on across seven years

blocks.text: Seven years of every mortgage application acted on in this county. [verified] — [the HMDA register](../../catalog/hmda-loan-application-register.md), 2018 through 2024.

**Half a billion dollars in 2020 and 2021, and half of that in 2023.** Lending doubled and fell back inside four years while the number of institutions barely moved. [verified] — same source. The denial rate ran the other way, from 14.0 per cent in 2020 to 23.7 in 2024, which is the highest of the seven. [verified]

**The corpus published "you can buy a house in Lima as easily as anywhere in this county" from the one year in seven where that was true.** Over 2018–2024 the purchase denial rate in Lima's tracts is 13.3 per cent against 10.8 elsewhere — 363 denials of 2,737 against 645 of 5,996 — and Lima's rate is the higher one in six of the seven years. [verified] — same source. The claim is withdrawn and replaced by the figures above; see [a rule is not a habit](../../decisions/a-rule-is-not-a-habit.yml).

**What survives the correction is the size of the difference, which was the real finding.** On everything but purchase, Lima's rate is 37.7 per cent against 21.5 — 1,104 denials of 2,926 against 2,000 of 9,289. The purchase gap is 2.5 percentage points and the other gap is 16.2, so the shape of the 2023 reading holds and its sharper half does not. [verified] — same source.

refusals: This does not establish why either gap is there.

nodes.label: Allen County mortgage applications and denials, 2023

properties.method: Rates use actions 1, 2 and 3 — originated, approved and declined, denied — and exclude the 388 withdrawn, 197 purchased and 93 closed for incompleteness, none of which is a decision about a borrower. [verified] "Lima tracts" is the sixteen of the county's thirty-five whose 2020 population is majority Lima; they hold 32,575 of the city's 35,579 people and 3,093 who live outside it. [verified] — [block assignment](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md). Nine rows carry no tract, seven of them decisions; those seven are in the county's totals and in neither column, which is why the columns sum to 2,599 and not 2,606. [verified]
properties.parameter: mortgage applications acted on, originations and denials

blocks.text: Every mortgage application acted on in Allen County in 2023, by purpose, by census tract and by the race the file records for the applicant. [verified] — [the HMDA register](../../catalog/hmda-loan-application-register.md). Of 3,294 rows, 2,606 are decisions about a borrower: 1,932 originated, 611 denied, 63 approved and declined. The county's denial rate is 23.4 per cent and $270.3 million was lent.
**In 2023 the purchase denial rate inside the city's tracts was 13.9 per cent and outside them 14.4, and every other purpose taken together was 42.9 against 27.6.** [verified] — same source.

**The sentence this node used to open that paragraph with is withdrawn.** It read *you can buy a house in Lima as easily as anywhere in this county*, with no year in it, and 2023 is the only one of seven in which Lima's purchase rate is the lower one. Over 2018–2024 it is 13.3 per cent against 10.8. [verified] — [seven years](allen-county-home-lending-2018-2024.yml). The figures above are unchanged and were never wrong; what was wrong was reading a year as a county. See [a rule is not a habit](../../decisions/a-rule-is-not-a-habit.yml).

**The reason the register gives is the house.** Twenty-one per cent of denials in Lima tracts cite collateral against 13 per cent elsewhere — 43 of 201 against 53 of 404 — where credit history leads in both at 43 and 45. [verified] Collateral is the property, and Lima's median house is worth $95,900 and was built in 1953. [verified] — [the stock](allen-county-housing-stock-2023.yml) and [its age](allen-county-housing-age-2023.yml). The median purchase loan originated in a Lima tract was $115,000 against $175,000 elsewhere, both medians of $10,000 bands. [verified]

**Applications from Black applicants were denied at 37.9 per cent and from white applicants at 22.6** — 66 of 174 against 458 of 2,023 — and the gap holds inside every income band the corpus cut. Under $50,000: 45.3 against 33.4. From $50,000 to $99,000: 38.0 against 20.5. At $100,000 and over: 25.6 against 15.8. [verified] — same source. Black applicants earning $50,000 to $99,000 were denied more often than white applicants earning under $50,000. [verified]

refusals: This does not establish that those applicants were treated differently.

properties.method: `Number of Beds` for CCNs 360009, 360066, 360263, 361322 and 362020. The total takes one row per hospital per year, which in FY2014 means Kindred's first row only — it filed twice that year across a change of fiscal year. [verified]
properties.parameter: Number of Beds

blocks.text: Beds reported by each of the county's five hospitals, every fiscal year from 2011 to 2023. [verified] — [CMS hospital cost reports](../../catalog/cms-hospital-cost-reports.md).

**The county's bed count fell 13 per cent and one hospital's fell 44.** [Lima Memorial](../organization/lima-memorial-health-system.yml) went from 195 beds to 110, with a low of 95 in 2019, while [St. Rita's](../organization/mercy-health-st-ritas-medical-center.yml) ended seven beds higher than it began. The three small hospitals never moved: twelve, twenty-five and twenty-six in all thirteen years. [verified]

**Beds and staff moved in opposite directions at the same hospital.** Lima Memorial lost 44 per cent of its beds and gained 28 per cent of its [full-time equivalents](allen-county-hospital-employment-2011-2023.yml) across the same thirteen years. [verified] — same source.

properties.method: CCNs 360009, 360066, 360263, 361322 and 362020 across the thirteen annual files — 66 rows. County totals sum the four calendar-year filers; [Kindred](../organization/kindred-hospital-lima.yml) left the calendar year after FY2013, so FY2014 holds two of its rows. [verified]
properties.parameter: FTE - Employees on Payroll

blocks.text: Full-time equivalents on payroll at each of the county's five hospitals. Thirteen fiscal years were read, 2011 to 2023; four are shown and every figure below is computed from all thirteen. [verified] — [CMS hospital cost reports](../../catalog/cms-hospital-cost-reports.md).

**The county's hospital employment fell 19 per cent, and one hospital fell by more than the whole.** The four calendar-year filers went from 3,598.20 to 2,913.00, a fall of 685.20; [St. Rita's](../organization/mercy-health-st-ritas-medical-center.yml) alone fell 1,019.08 while [Lima Memorial](../organization/lima-memorial-health-system.yml) rose 278.89 and [the Institute](../organization/institute-for-orthopaedic-surgery.yml) rose 74.05. [verified] Most of St. Rita's drop — 625 — is on the FY2013/FY2014 boundary, where it began filing as an LLC, and is not only employment. [inference]

A full-time equivalent is not an employee, so no figure here may be subtracted from [County Business Patterns](allen-county-health-care-employment-2010-2022.yml), which counts people on a payroll: 3,677 FTE against 4,848 employees in 2011, 2,990 against 3,211 in 2022. [verified]

nodes.label: When Allen County's housing was built, 2023

properties.method: Shares are computed here from published counts; the medians are published. [verified] The bands describe *surviving* housing, so a low count for an early decade is demolition and construction together and cannot be read as construction alone. [inference]
properties.parameter: housing units by year structure built (B25034) and median year built (B25035)

blocks.text: The year the county's standing housing was built, by band, for the county and for each of its thirteen civil subdivisions. [verified] — [American Community Survey](../../catalog/census-acs-summary-file.md), 2023 five-year estimates, table B25034. All eleven bands close exactly against the county's own row.

**The county's biggest building decade was the 1970s**, 8,298 units ± 585 against 6,529 ± 563 for the 1950s. Only "1939 or earlier" holds more, and that band is not a decade — it is everything before one. [verified] — same source.

**Six thousand three hundred and thirty-three of those 8,298 were built outside Lima.** The city took 1,965 of the decade in which it reached its own peak of 53,734 and held 48.4 per cent of the county. [verified] — the table and [the city and the rest](allen-county-outside-lima-1890-2020.yml). The ring was built while the city was full, not after it emptied. [inference]

**The median house in Lima was built in 1953 and the median house in Bath Township in 1975.** Shawnee and American are 1973. Lima is 34.9 per cent pre-1940 where the three townships that ring it are between 6.4 and 7.1. [verified] Marion at 37.0 per cent and Richland at 38.0 read higher than Lima and this does not establish that they are older: 1,069 ± 235 of 2,886 ± 242 and 930 ± 195 of 2,449 ± 168 leave all three indistinguishable. [verified]

**11,327 units of this county's standing housing were built in 1980 or later**, a quarter of the whole, and the county fell from 112,241 to 100,866 over the same span. [verified] — the table and [the county](../place/allen-county.yml). The two are not a ratio and nothing here divides them — one counts dwellings still standing and the other people — but a county losing eleven thousand people built a quarter of its housing while doing it.

refusals: Marion at 37.0 per cent and Richland at 38.0 read higher than Lima and this does not establish that they are older: 1,069 ± 235 of 2,886 ± 242 and 930 ± 195 of 2,449 ± 168 leave all three indistinguishable.
This does not establish why the housing was built where it was.

nodes.label: Allen County housing units, occupancy, tenure and value, 2023

properties.method: Tables B25002, B25003, B25077 and B25064 of the 2023 five-year file, joined on `GEO_ID`. Shares are computed here and medians are published. [verified] Owner-occupancy is of *occupied* units, so its denominator is 40,928 and not 44,697.
properties.parameter: housing units, occupancy status, tenure, median value and median gross rent

blocks.text: Housing units, vacancy, owner-occupancy, median value and median gross rent for the county, its thirteen civil subdivisions, the state and the nation. [verified] — [American Community Survey](../../catalog/census-acs-summary-file.md), 2023 five-year estimates.

**The county looks American and neither of its halves does.** Allen County is 68.3 per cent owner-occupied against 65.0 nationally — an unremarkable figure made of Lima at 46.4 per cent and twelve townships between 72.0 and 91.0, the city being the only subdivision below 70. [verified] — same source.

**Lima holds 35.4 per cent of the county's housing and 48.2 per cent of its empty housing**, 1,817 vacant units of 3,769. [verified] Four figures close exactly against the county's own row — 44,697 units, 40,928 occupied, 3,769 vacant, 27,960 owner-occupied — so the thirteen subdivisions partition the county four more times. [verified]

**A house in Shawnee Township is worth 2.2 times a house in Lima**, $210,200 against $95,900, on a combined margin of $17,965 for a gap of $114,300; the city's median value is 31.6 per cent of the nation's. [verified]

Perry Township's 17.0 per cent is the highest figure in the vacancy column, and this does not establish that it is the county's emptiest place: 290 vacant units ± 130 puts the rate between 9.4 and 24.7 per cent, straddling Lima's 11.5. [verified] The dashes are the file's unavailable-value sentinel and not a low rent. See [a survey is not a count](../../decisions/a-survey-is-not-a-count.yml).

refusals: Perry Township's 17.0 per cent is the highest figure in the vacancy column, and this does not establish that it is the county's emptiest place: 290 vacant units ± 130 puts the rate between 9.4 and 24.7 per cent, straddling Lima's 11.5.

nodes.label: Allen County housing units, 2020 census

properties.method: Sum of block-level `HU100` from the 2020 Census redistricting file, as served by TIGERweb. Total units, occupied and vacant together. [verified]
properties.parameter: total housing units

blocks.text: The county's total housing units at the 2020 census, summed over all 3,552 blocks. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md), 2020 vintage block layer, field `HU100`.

Against [the enumeration](allen-county-population-2020-census.yml) of 102,206 that is 2.29 people per housing unit. The figure varies across the county's thirteen civil subdivisions from 2.19 in [Lima](../place/lima.yml) and [American Township](../place/american-township.yml) to 2.57 in [Amanda](../place/amanda-township.yml) and [Richland](../place/richland-township.yml). [verified] — same source, by block composition.

refusals: Until then this corpus can say how many units there are and how many people, and cannot say how many are lived in — which matters for a county whose [population has been falling for fifty years](../period/depopulation.yml).

nodes.label: Allen County household income and poverty, 2023

properties.method: 2023 five-year estimates from the table-based summary file. The twelve townships and Lima are county-subdivision and place summary levels and partition the county: they sum to 101,685 people and 12,815 below poverty, both equal to the county row. Margins are as published, at 90 per cent; combined margins are the root of the sum of squares. [verified]
properties.parameter: median household income (B19013) and poverty status (B17001)

blocks.text: Median household income and the share of people below the poverty line, for the county, its thirteen civil subdivisions, the state and the nation. [verified] — [American Community Survey](../../catalog/census-acs-summary-file.md), 2023 five-year estimates.

**Lima holds a third of the county's people and two thirds of its poor.** 35,304 of 101,685 residents — 34.7 per cent — and 8,214 of the 12,815 people below the poverty line, or 64.1 per cent. [verified] — same source. The county's twelve townships hold the other 4,601, and the two sums are exactly the county's own figures.

**Its median household income is 48 per cent of the township next door.** $43,370 against Shawnee Township's $91,134, a gap of $47,764 against a combined margin of $6,359. [verified] — same source. Against the nation it is 55 per cent, and against the county 70. [verified]

This does not establish that Lima has the lowest household income in the county. Perry Township's $53,272 is higher by $9,902 against a combined margin of $11,142, so the two cannot be ordered here. [verified] Nor is the county distinguishable from the state on poverty: 13.1 per cent against 13.2, against a combined margin of 1.2 points. [verified]

refusals: This does not establish that Lima has the lowest household income in the county.

properties.method: Computed by the Census Bureau from the 2020 TIGER geography. A county's land area is not fixed across geographies — a later vintage may differ. [verified]
properties.parameter: land area

blocks.text: Land area of Allen County in the 2020 geography. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), national county file, field `ALAND_SQMI`. Water area is a further 4.306 square miles. [verified] — same record.
At the [2020 population base](allen-county-population-2020.yml) this is about 254 persons per square mile of land. [inference] — arithmetic this corpus's.

nodes.label: Allen County mortgage denial rates by applicant race, 2018-2024

properties.method: Rates use actions 1, 2 and 3. Race is the register's `derived_race`; 18 per cent of rows record none and are in no column here. Debt-to-income is grouped from a column that reports integers from 36 to 49 and bands elsewhere. Cells with fewer than ten white applications are dropped, which discards 17 per cent of Black applications rather than resting a rate on one or two files. [verified] Expected denials are the sum of the within-cell white rates over the matched Black applications; the standard deviation is that of the Poisson-binomial they define.
properties.parameter: mortgage denial rate by applicant race, and by race within four controls
properties.unit: ratio of observed to expected denials for Black applicants

blocks.text: Denial rates for the two races the register records in numbers this county can support, across seven years and inside every control the file carries. [verified] — [the HMDA register](../../catalog/hmda-loan-application-register.md).

**It is a pattern and not a year.** Pooled over the seven, 32.4 per cent of applications from Black applicants were denied against 17.8 per cent from white applicants, and the yearly gap runs between 5.9 and 17.0 percentage points without once reversing. [verified] — same source. The corpus opened this question saying 174 applications was one year of a small county; it is now 1,334 applications and 432 denials.

**It survives every control this register carries, taken one at a time.** Twenty-three strata across four dimensions — loan purpose, applicant income, debt-to-income and loan-to-value — and the gap is positive in all twenty-three. [verified] It is 7.7 points on a home purchase and 24.1 on a home improvement loan; 10.4 points under $30,000 of income and 4.6 above $150,000; 30.4 points in the lowest debt-to-income band and 1.1 in the 43-to-49 band; 23.0 points below 60 per cent loan-to-value and 3.3 between 90 and 100. The gap is widest where denial is rarest and compresses where it is common, which is what a ceiling does to a difference and not a finding about risk. [inference]

**Taken together rather than one at a time, it is a factor of 1.68.** Sorting every decision into a cell of loan purpose by income band by debt-to-income band by loan-to-value band gives 311 cells holding 955 Black applications — 83 per cent of those with all four controls present — in which at least ten white applications also sit. Those 955 drew **223 denials against 132.5 expected at the white rate in the same cells**, a ratio of 1.68 and 9.3 standard deviations from the null. [verified] — computed here from the same source. The same arithmetic run on white applications returns exactly 1.00, which is the check that it is arithmetic and not a thumb.

**Composition is real and it is small.** Inside those 311 cells the unadjusted rates are 23.4 per cent against 12.2, a gap of 11.1 points; reweighting the white rate to the Black applicants' own mix of loan purpose, income, debt and equity moves the comparison to 13.9, which closes 15 per cent of it. [verified] Black applicants in this county do apply for different loans on different terms, and that is not most of the difference.

refusals: This does not establish that any applicant was treated differently.

properties.method: Census of Agriculture, inventory taken at December 31 of the census year and sales for the calendar year, read from NASS's Quick Stats bulk county file and checked against the published county profile, which prints the same 2022 and 2017 inventories. `(D)` marks a cell NASS suppressed to avoid disclosing an individual operation and is not a small number; nothing here infers a value for one. Comparisons to 1910 set a count of animals on farms and off them against a count on farms alone, which in 1910 differed by about one per cent for swine. [inference]
properties.parameter: livestock inventory, Allen County

blocks.text: What the county keeps, and how few places keep it. [verified] — [USDA Census of Agriculture](../../catalog/usda-census-of-agriculture.md), county files.

**The hogs multiplied more than sevenfold while the places keeping them halved.** 31,741 head on 59 operations in 2002 against 235,800 on 28 in 2022 — an average herd of 538 becoming one of 8,421. [inference] — computed here from the five censuses. Nothing else moved: cattle ended where they began, and sheep, horses and milk cows are where they were or lower.
**The count, five censuses in one line.** 31,741 hogs in 2002, 62,910 in 2007, 80,372 in 2012, 178,781 in 2017 and 235,800 in 2022, kept on 59, 60, 46, 56 and 28 operations. [verified] — same source.

**Three quarters of the hogs sold were raised for someone else.** Of 377,816 head sold in 2022, 281,194 were produced under production contract on twelve operations — the census's own term for an animal fed by one party and owned by another. [verified] — same source. In 2017 it was 144,480 of 324,947 on twenty-one operations, so the contracted share went from 44 to 74 per cent while the number of operations doing it fell by nine.

**Hogs are now two fifths of everything the county sells.** $75,254,000 of $240,849,000, against $7,488,000 of $41,264,000 in 2002. [verified] — same source. The county ranks 4th in Ohio for hog sales and 23rd for agricultural sales altogether. [verified] — [the 2022 county profile](../../catalog/usda-census-of-agriculture.md).

**Against 1910: the swine outnumbered the people then by 59,695 to 56,580, and now by 235,800 to 100,866.** [inference] — computed here from [the 1910 animals](allen-county-domestic-animals-1910.yml) and [the 2024 estimate](allen-county-population-2024.yml). Two and a third hogs a head, where there had been one and a twentieth.

**Everything else in that 1910 count is gone.** 14,676 horses became 316; 41,240 sheep and goats became 1,499; 21,336 cattle became 8,576; and the 10,671 dairy cows became a figure the census will not print, because eight operations hold it and one of them is large enough that publishing the total would disclose it. [verified] — same sources, and Appendix A, which states the suppression rules. This corpus withholds figures for the same reason and by hand; see [what may leave the repository](../../decisions/what-may-leave-the-repository.yml).

properties.method: BEA CAEMP25S for 1969–2000 (SIC line 400) and CAEMP25N for 2001–2022 (NAICS line 500), read from the Ohio county files at GeoFIPS 39003. BEA counts jobs, including proprietors, part-time work, farm and government, where County Business Patterns counts employees of private establishments; the two are separate programmes and not one series. They agree on shape where they overlap, both placing the recent trough at the end of the 2000s and a recovery of about a fifth since. [verified]
properties.parameter: manufacturing employment, Allen County, all jobs

blocks.text: Fifty-four years of the mechanism this county's history is told through. [verified] — [BEA Regional Economic Accounts](../../catalog/bea-county-employment.md), county employment by industry.

**Manufacturing employment in Allen County peaked in 1973, at 18,400.** [verified] — same source. Not in 1969, and not before this corpus's [deindustrialization](../period/deindustrialization.yml) is said to begin. The county's factories were still adding workers into the late 1970s: 18,389 in 1979, within eleven of the peak six years earlier.

**The trough is 7,775, in 2009 — a fall of 58 per cent from the peak, across thirty-six years.** [verified] — same source. Employment has risen since, to 8,715 in 2022, and has not been below 7,775 in any year on this series.

**1986 was a recovery year, not a stage of the fall.** Manufacturing bottomed at 14,349 in 1982, rose four years running to 17,163 in 1986, and only then began the long decline. [verified] — same source. That matters because it is where [the corpus's other series](allen-county-manufacturing-employment-1986-2022.yml) opens, and because the last phase described this span, while calling it open, as a fall already under way. See [naming a gap is not leaving it empty](../../decisions/naming-a-gap-is-not-leaving-it-empty.yml).
**Almost the whole decline is after 1986.** From the 1973 peak to 1986 manufacturing lost 1,237 jobs, 7 per cent; from 1986 to 2009 it lost 9,388, 55 per cent. [inference] — computed here.

properties.method: County Business Patterns county files, one year in five from 1986. Checked by arithmetic self-closure: in 1986 the ten SIC divisions sum to the printed county total exactly, and in 2022 the twenty NAICS sectors do the same. Years between leave residuals of 2 to 239, each year carrying at least one sector with suppressed employment. Corroborated at the recent end by [the QCEW](../../catalog/bls-qcew.md), which gives 8,661 for 2023 against 8,573 for 2022. Government, the self-employed and farms are excluded throughout. [verified]
properties.parameter: manufacturing employment, Allen County, private employers

blocks.text: The measurement this corpus named a period after and did not have. [verified] — [County Business Patterns](../../catalog/census-county-business-patterns.md), private employers.

**Manufacturing employment in Allen County fell by 55 per cent between 1986 and 2010, from 15,762 to 7,127.** [verified] — same source. That is [deindustrialization](../period/deindustrialization.yml) measured for the first time in this corpus, in the period named for it.

**And then it stopped, and reversed.** From the 2010 trough manufacturing rose to 8,917 in 2020 and stood at 8,573 in 2022 — up a fifth from the bottom. [verified] — same source. The county's named mechanism of decline stopped operating around 2010 and the county kept shrinking. [inference]

**Total private employment peaked in 2005, not in 1986.** It rose from 45,917 to 52,699 while manufacturing was losing six thousand jobs, then fell to 42,814 by 2022. [verified] — same source. So the county replaced its manufacturing losses for twenty years and stopped being able to. [inference]

**After 2010 the losses were not in manufacturing.** Private employment fell 3,709 between 2010 and 2022 while manufacturing *rose* 1,446, so everything else fell by 5,155. [inference] — computed here.

**The sentence that stood here was wrong and is the reason this node is no longer the corpus's main employment series.** It said County Business Patterns "begins in 1986 with manufacturing already at 15,762 and already falling", and called this "the second half of a fall". A BEA series reaching back to 1969 shows 1986 as a recovery year — manufacturing bottomed at 14,349 in 1982 and had climbed four years running by 1986 — and shows the peak at 18,400 in 1973. [verified] — [the long series](allen-county-manufacturing-employment-1969-2022.yml). Nor was it the second half: 93 per cent of the fall from peak to trough happened after 1986. [inference] See [naming a gap is not leaving it empty](../../decisions/naming-a-gap-is-not-leaving-it-empty.yml).

properties.method: Births minus deaths, summed over the four full estimate years 2021–2024. The partial year 2020 — April to June, 293 births and 283 deaths — is excluded as not comparable. [verified]
properties.parameter: natural population change, four years to 2024

blocks.text: Across the four full years 2021 to 2024 the county recorded **4,763 births and 5,269 deaths** — a natural change of **−506**. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), county file, fields `BIRTHS` and `DEATHS`.
Year by year the natural change was −213, −259, −41 and **+7**: deaths exceeded births in 2021, 2022 and 2023, and births exceeded deaths again in 2024. [verified] — same source.

**Deaths moved and births did not.** Births ran 1,171, 1,190, 1,202 and 1,200 — flat within three per cent. Deaths ran 1,384, 1,449, 1,243 and 1,193, peaking in 2022 and falling by 256 over the following two years. So the natural decrease of these four years is a deaths story, and the shape of it — a spike in 2021–2022 subsiding by 2024 — is the shape the pandemic left in county death counts across the United States. [inference] The corpus holds no cause-of-death data and cannot attribute it.

properties.method: Domestic plus international net migration, summed over the four full estimate years 2021–2024. The partial year 2020 is excluded as not comparable. [verified]
properties.parameter: net migration, four years to 2024

blocks.text: Across the four full years 2021 to 2024 the county's net migration was **−793**: a domestic net loss of **1,217** against an international net gain of **424**. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), county file, fields `DOMESTICMIG` and `INTERNATIONALMIG`.

**The two components move in opposite directions and one of them is accelerating.** International migration ran 26, 100, 133 and 165 — rising every year without exception. Domestic migration ran −213, −530, −317 and −157, worst in 2022 and shrinking since. [verified] — same source.

In 2024 they crossed: 165 arriving from abroad against 157 leaving for elsewhere in the United States, for a net migration of **+8** — the first non-negative year in the series. [verified] — same source.
